title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試録序
我
皇上求賢圖治
詔天下鄉試于茲三開科矣四
川連年盜警
上廑西顧之憂鎮守太監常〔興〕宅
===
心鎮靖軍民安之近以功未
告成
上命太子少保右都御史彭〔澤〕代
洪〔鍾〕總制右僉都御史馬〔昊〕
代高〔崇熈〕巡撫其提督軍務
則
punctuated:
四川鄉試録序

我皇上求賢圖治，詔天下鄉試，于茲三開科矣。四川連年盜警，上廑西顧之憂。鎮守太監常〔興〕宅心鎮靖，軍民安之。近以功未告成，上命太子少保右都御史彭〔澤〕代洪〔鍾〕總制，右僉都御史馬〔昊〕代高〔崇熈〕巡撫。其提督軍務，則
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

Our Emperor seeks worthy men and strives for good government. He has decreed that Provincial Examinations be held throughout the realm; this now marks the third occasion on which they have been convened.

For successive years, Sichuan has faced alarms caused by banditry, burdening His Majesty with concern as he looks westward. The Regional Defender, Grand Eunuch Chang Xing 常興, has devoted himself to restoring peace, and the soldiers and civilians have found security under him. Recently, because the task had not yet been brought to completion, His Majesty ordered Peng Ze 彭澤, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Right Censor-in-Chief, to replace Hong Zhong 洪鍾 as Supreme Commander, and Ma Hao 馬昊, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, to replace Gao Chongxi 高崇熈 as Grand Coordinator. As for the supervision of military affairs, …

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
命平賊將軍右都督時〔源〕取總
兵官楊〔宏〕回而以都督僉事
陳〔珣〕代之及遊擊將軍閻〔勲〕
總領騎步官兵〔澤〕與〔昊〕宣布
朝廷恩威政令維新軍容載肅
巡按監察御史王〔鏜〕所至剔
===
蠹剗弊風裁凜然紀功給事
中王〔萱〕監察御史何〔棐〕汪〔景〕
芳申嚴軍法脩明憲度三軍
戮力率協郎員外郎張〔嘉〕
謨馮〔馴〕主事馬〔應龍〕劉〔琛〕特
以戎務來主事張〔元電〕適以
punctuated: 命平賊將軍右都督時〔源〕取總兵官楊〔宏〕回，而以都督僉事陳〔珣〕代之，及遊擊將軍閻〔勲〕總領騎步官兵。〔澤〕與〔昊〕宣布朝廷恩威，政令維新，軍容載肅。巡按監察御史王〔鏜〕所至剔蠹剗弊，風裁凜然。紀功給事中王〔萱〕、監察御史何〔棐〕、汪〔景〕芳申嚴軍法，脩明憲度，三軍戮力率協。郎員外郎張〔嘉〕謨、馮〔馴〕，主事馬〔應龍〕、劉〔琛〕，特以戎務來。主事張〔元電〕適以
translation_en: …[the Emperor] ordered Shi Yuan, General for Pacifying the Bandits and Right Chief Military Commissioner, to recall Regional Commander Yang Hong and replace him with Assistant Chief Military Commissioner Chen Xun, who, together with Mobile Corps General Yan Xun, was to take overall command of the cavalry and infantry officers and troops. Peng Ze and Ma Hao proclaimed the court’s benevolence and authority; administrative commands were renewed, and military discipline was restored. Wherever Regional Inspector Wang Tang went, he rooted out corruption and eliminated abuses, displaying an awe-inspiring rigor. Supervising Secretary Wang Xuan, charged with recording military merit, and Investigating Censors He Fei and Wang Jingfang reiterated the strict enforcement of military law and put regulations in good order. The armies exerted themselves in concert and worked together. Vice Directors Zhang Jiamo and Feng Xun [preceding 郎 unclear, ?], and Secretaries Ma Yinglong and Liu Chen, came expressly on military business. Secretary Zhang Yuandian happened, on account of …

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
公務至亦皆殫厥心力出謀
賛襄用是連獲渠兇地方恃
以無恐先是
廷試蜀有擢進士第一者士皆
益相淬厲以倫魁自期雖經
兵發不廢所業或率捍禦鄉
===
邑賴之儒有忠信爲甲冑禮
義爲干櫓信非虛也正德癸
酉八月四川鄉試御史〔鏜寔〕
當監臨申飭舊規舉事惟謹
乃謀諸藩臬長貳預聘〔宗大〕
等適至與教諭丘〔茂揆〕司考
punctuated:
公務至，亦皆殫厥心力，出謀賛襄，用是連獲渠兇，地方恃以無恐。先是，廷試蜀有擢進士第一者，士皆益相淬厲，以倫魁自期。雖經兵發，不廢所業，或率捍禦，鄉邑賴之。儒有忠信爲甲冑，禮義爲干櫓，信非虛也。
正德癸酉八月，四川鄉試，御史〔鏜寔〕當監臨，申飭舊規，舉事惟謹。乃謀諸藩臬長貳，預聘〔宗大〕等，適至，與教諭丘〔茂揆〕司考
translation_en:
…arrived on official business; all likewise devoted their utmost thought and effort, offering plans and assistance. Consequently, successive captures of the chief malefactors enabled the locality to rest free from fear. Before this, a man from Sichuan had been ranked first among the metropolitan graduates (jinshi) at the Palace Examination. The scholars all spurred one another to still greater effort, each aspiring to head his cohort. Even when fighting broke out, they did not abandon their studies; some led defensive efforts on which their home communities depended. That Confucian scholars have loyalty and trustworthiness as their armor and helmets, and ritual propriety and righteousness as their shields, is indeed no empty saying.
In the eighth month of the guiyou year of Zhengde [1513], at the Sichuan Provincial Examination, Censor Tang was indeed serving as Supervising Official. He reaffirmed the existing regulations and conducted every matter with care. He then consulted the heads and deputies of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions and invited Zongda and others in advance. They arrived in time to serve together with Qiu Maokui, Instructor, in overseeing the examination…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
試而同考則學正魏〔鎧〕鄭〔維〕
新〔教諭張舜舉吳鎧李惟貞〕
白〔繡〕訓導王〔瑜〕內而提調則
左布政使〔上倬〕左參政邵〔賁〕
監試則按察使謝〔朝宣〕副使
王〔時中〕外而防範則右布政
===
使胡〔宗道〕參政吳〔晟〕何〔珊〕參
議盧〔綸〕張〔諾〕郭〔韶〕副使張〔敏〕
李〔鉞〕楊〔惟康〕陶〔照〕盧〔翊〕王〔綸〕
曹〔䆟〕僉事郝〔綰〕戴〔書〕程〔銈〕郭
東山張〔繹〕張〔秉清〕楊〔邦禎〕至
百執事咸慎選以充甲辰鎖
punctuated: 試，而同考則學正魏〔鎧〕、鄭〔維〕新〔教諭張舜舉吳鎧李惟貞〕、白〔繡〕、訓導王〔瑜〕。內而提調則左布政使〔上倬〕、左參政邵〔賁〕；監試則按察使謝〔朝宣〕、副使王〔時中〕。外而防範則右布政使胡〔宗道〕、參政吳〔晟〕、何〔珊〕、參議盧〔綸〕、張〔諾〕、郭〔韶〕、副使張〔敏〕、李〔鉞〕、楊〔惟康〕、陶〔照〕、盧〔翊〕、王〔綸〕、曹〔䆟〕、僉事郝〔綰〕、戴〔書〕、程〔銈〕、郭東山、張〔繹〕、張〔秉清〕、楊〔邦禎〕。至百執事，咸慎選以充。甲辰，鎖
translation_en:
…conducted the examination. The Associate Examiners were the school instructors Wei Kai and Zheng Weixin; the instructors Zhang Shunju, Wu Kai, and Li Weizhen, listed in an interlinear annotation; Bai Xiu; and the assistant instructor Wang Yu. Within the examination compound, the Proctors were the Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Shang Zhuo [?] and the Left Administration Vice Commissioner Shao Ben. Oversight of the examination was entrusted to Surveillance Commissioner Xie Chaoxuan and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wang Shizhong.

Outside the compound, security was entrusted to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Hu Zongdao; Administration Vice Commissioners Wu Sheng and He Shan; Administration Assistant Commissioners Lu Lun, Zhang Nuo, and Guo Shao; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhang Min, Li Yue, Yang Weikang, Tao Zhao, Lu Yi, Wang Lun, and Cao Ke [?]; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Hao Wan, Dai Shu, Cheng Ji, Guo Dongshan, Zhang Yi, Zhang Bingqing, and Yang Bangzhen. All the subordinate functionaries, too, were carefully selected to fill their posts. On the jiachen day, the examination compound was locked…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
院合提學副使王〔崇文〕精簡
之士一千四百而三試之得
七十人餘雖優不敢過取遵
制額也爰列其名次及梓其文二
十篇爲錄以
獻〔宗大〕當序諸首簡竊惟
===
國家氣運之隆必有賢才之出
而事功之成必其學術之正
古今同一道也蜀之賢科在
唐猶未著閒以宋登科記考
之倫如蘇易簡陳堯叟堯
咨馬涓何㮚趙逵屈指可數
punctuated:
院，合提學副使王〔崇文〕精簡之士一千四百，而三試之，得七十人。餘雖優，不敢過取，遵制額也。爰列其名次，及梓其文二十篇爲錄，以獻。〔宗大〕當序諸首簡，竊惟：
國家氣運之隆，必有賢才之出；而事功之成，必其學術之正。古今同一道也。蜀之賢科，在唐猶未著。閒以宋登科記考之，倫如蘇易簡、陳堯叟、堯咨、馬涓、何㮚、趙逵，屈指可數。
translation_en:
…the examination compound. The 1,400 candidates carefully selected by Wang Chongwen 王崇文, Education Intendant and Surveillance Vice Commissioner, were assembled and examined in three sessions, yielding seventy successful candidates. Although others were excellent, we dared not admit more, observing the prescribed quota. We therefore listed their names in order of rank and had twenty of their essays printed as a record for presentation to the throne. I, Zongda 宗大, am charged with writing a preface for its opening pages. I humbly reflect:
When the fortunes of the state flourish, worthy talent must emerge; and the accomplishment of public achievements necessarily depends upon correctness in learning. This principle is the same in ancient and modern times. The examination success of worthy men from Shu was not yet conspicuous under the Tang. On occasion, consulting the Song Records of Examination Graduates, I find such men as [?] Su Yijian 蘇易簡, Chen Yaosou 陳堯叟, Chen Yaozi 堯咨, Ma Juan 馬涓, He Li 何㮚, and Zhao Kui 趙逵—few enough to count on one’s fingers…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
為其間如范鎮蘇軾張浚輩
拭魏了翁虞集當時學術事
功至今稱之我
皇明興圖之廣過于前朝
祖宗教化之功洽于累世今蜀賢
相名臣布列中外本之學術
===
著之事功後先相望以一方
而槩天下何其盛也然蜀之
倫魁百四十餘年僅一見之
豈古今殊哉倫魁之出氣運
之洽也安知異日不如叟如
洛如涓如臬如逵踵其後乎
punctuated: 為其間如范鎮、蘇軾、張浚、輩拭、魏了翁、虞集，當時學術事功，至今稱之。我皇明興，圖之廣過于前朝，祖宗教化之功洽于累世。今蜀賢相名臣布列中外，本之學術，著之事功，後先相望。以一方而槩天下，何其盛也！然蜀之倫魁，百四十餘年僅一見之，豈古今殊哉？倫魁之出，氣運之洽也。安知異日不如叟、如洛、如涓、如臬、如逵踵其後乎？
translation_en:
…among them were such figures as Fan Zhen, Su Shi, Zhang Jun, Bei Shi [?], Wei Liaoweng, and Yu Ji, whose scholarship and accomplishments in their day are praised even now. With the rise of our august Ming dynasty, its territorial extent surpassed that of preceding dynasties, and the transforming influence of our imperial ancestors’ teaching spread through successive generations. Today, worthy chief councilors and renowned ministers from Shu fill posts at court and in the provinces. Grounded in scholarship and distinguished by their accomplishments, they have followed one another in succession. Taking this one region as an indication of the whole realm, how flourishing it is!

Yet in more than 140 years, Shu has produced a first-place examination graduate only once. Can ancient and modern times really be so different? The emergence of such a graduate comes when the vital forces and fortunes of the age reach harmonious fullness. How can we know that, in days to come, men like Sou [Chen Yaosou], Luo [?], Juan [Ma Juan], Nie [?], and Kui [Zhao Kui] will not follow in their footsteps?

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
諸士子際此
隆盛之時育之以學校拔之于
科目行將試
南宫奉
廷對不以倫魁望不以事功期
乎期事功奚必博求天下蜀
===
之賢自可法也事道學則栻
了翁其人事詞翰則軾集其
人事輔世則有鎮其人事捄
時則有浚其人之數君子純
乎毋以議為但事功成就之
小大繫乎學術之淺深皆非

人事輔世則有鎮其人事捄

punctuated: 諸士子際此隆盛之時，育之以學校，拔之于科目，行將試南宫，奉廷對，不以倫魁望，不以事功期乎？期事功，奚必博求天下？蜀之賢自可法也。事道學，則栻、了翁其人；事詞翰，則軾、集其人；事輔世，則有鎮其人；事捄時，則有浚其人。之數君子純乎？毋以議為。但事功成就之小大，繫乎學術之淺深，皆非
translation_en: You candidates live in this flourishing age, nurtured in the schools and selected through the examinations. Soon you will sit the Metropolitan Examination and respectfully present your answers at court. Should we not look to you to take the highest honors and expect you to accomplish great deeds? In seeking models of accomplishment, why must you search throughout the realm? The worthy men of Shu themselves offer examples to emulate. For devotion to the Learning of the Way, there are Shi 栻 and Liaoweng 了翁; for literary composition, Shi 軾 and Ji 集; for service in sustaining the age, Zhen 鎮; and for rescuing the age from its troubles, Jun 浚. Were these several gentlemen wholly pure? Let us not debate this [?]. Yet the greatness or smallness of their accomplishments depended upon the depth or shallowness of their learning; none were …

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
當時可及而今人所當取法
焉者特爲諸士子言耳載稽
圖誌廣柔石紐村神禹生焉
禹實蜀人　嘗讀虞夏之書見
其精一執中得堯舜心法之
傳其治水也地平天成有萬
===
世永賴之功禹之學術何如
其學術禹之事功何如其事
功也等而上之尚其法禹乎
哉故曰塗人皆可以爲禹　宗
大喜四川是科得人因推本
祖宗教化之功及
punctuated: 當時可及，而今人所當取法焉者，特爲諸士子言耳。載稽圖誌，廣柔石紐村，神禹生焉。禹實蜀人。嘗讀《虞夏之書》，見其精一執中，得堯舜心法之傳；其治水也，地平天成，有萬世永賴之功。禹之學術何如其學術，禹之事功何如其事功也？等而上之，尚其法禹乎哉！故曰：「塗人皆可以爲禹。」宗大喜四川是科得人，因推本祖宗教化之功及
translation_en: … matched by their contemporaries, and whom people today ought to take as models. I say this especially for the examination candidates. Consulting geographical records further, I find that the divine Yu was born in Shiniu village, Guangrou. Yu was indeed a man of Shu. Reading the Books of Yu and Xia, I have seen how, through refinement and single-mindedness, he held fast to the Mean and received the transmission of the teachings of Yao and Shun concerning the mind. In controlling the waters, he brought the land into order and Heaven’s work to completion, accomplishing something upon which ten thousand generations would forever depend. Compared with Yu’s learning, how did their learning measure up? Compared with Yu’s achievements, how did theirs measure up? Ascending still higher, should you not take Yu as your model! Thus it is said: “Any person in the street can become a Yu.” I, Zongda, rejoice that Sichuan has obtained worthy men in this examination, and accordingly trace this success to the transforming instruction of our imperial ancestors and to …

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
今日氣運之盛諸士子行當勉
旃幸毋自棄于塗人也
山東登州府儒學教授陳宗
大
謹序
punctuated:
今日氣運之盛。諸士子行當勉旃，幸毋自棄于塗人也。

山東登州府儒學教授陳宗大謹序。
translation_en:
…the flourishing fortunes of the present day. You scholars should henceforth exert yourselves; I hope you will not abandon your aspirations and remain ordinary men.

Preface respectfully composed by Chen Zongda, Instructor in the Confucian School of Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong.

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
正德八年四川鄉試
監臨官
巡按四川監察御史王鏜〔彥聲金吾右衛 官籍直隸徐州人乙丑進士〕
提調官
四川等處承宣布政使司左布政使王倬〔用檢直隸太倉州人 戊戌進士〕
四川等處承宣布政使司左參政邵蕡〔文實浙江餘姚縣人 庚戌進士〕
監試官
四川等處提刑按察司按察使謝朝宣〔汝爲陝西西安左衛籍 直隸臨淮縣人癸丑進士〕
四川等處提刑按察司副使王時中〔道夫山東黄縣人 庚戌進士〕
===
考試官
山東登州府儒學教授陳宗大〔景輝福建閩縣人 己酉貢士〕
山東濟南府德平縣儒學教諭岳茂抶〔君鼎福建莆田縣人 丁卯貢士〕
同考試官
河南河南府陜州儒學學正魏鏜〔楊武山西平定州人 庚午貢士〕
山東兖州府東平州儒學學正鄭維新〔敬甫廣東歸善縣人 甲子貢士〕
湖廣黄州府麻城縣儒學教諭張舜舉〔邦献陝西武功縣人 甲子貢士〕
江西饒州府餘干縣儒學教諭吳鎧〔廷儀湖廣武陵縣人 丙午貢士〕
浙江金華府浦江縣儒學教諭李惟貞〔起元直隸太倉州人 甲子貢士〕
punctuated:
正德八年四川鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按四川監察御史王鏜〔彥聲，金吾右衛官籍，直隸徐州人，乙丑進士〕。

提調官：

施之未能也庸德之行庸言之謹有所
不足不敢不勉有餘不敢盡言顧行行
顧言君子胡不慥慥爾
===
仁人之安宅也義人之正路也
易
坤至柔而動也剛至靜而德方
觀其所恒而天地萬物之情可見矣
易有聖人之道四焉者此之謂也
易之爲書也廣大悉備有天道焉有人道
焉有地道焉兼三才而兩之故六六者
非他也三才之道也
書
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

立不中門，行不履閾。

君子之道四，丘未能一焉：所求乎子，以事父，未能也；所求乎臣，以事君，未能也；所求乎弟，以事兄，未能也；所求乎朋友，先施之，未能也。庸德之行，庸言之謹，有所不足，不敢不勉；有餘，不敢盡。言顧行，行顧言，君子胡不慥慥爾！

仁，人之安宅也；義，人之正路也。

易

坤至柔，而動也剛；至靜，而德方。

觀其所恒，而天地萬物之情可見矣。

易有聖人之道四焉者，此之謂也。

易之爲書也，廣大悉備，有天道焉，有人道焉，有地道焉。兼三才而兩之，故六。六者，非他也，三才之道也。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

He did not stand in the middle of the doorway, nor step on the threshold when walking.

There are four aspects of the way of the gentleman, yet I, Qiu, have not been able to fulfill even one. To serve my father as I would require a son to serve me—I have not been able to do this. To serve my ruler as I would require a minister to serve me—I have not been able to do this. To serve my elder brother as I would require a younger brother to serve me—I have not been able to do this. To take the initiative in treating friends as I would require them to treat me—I have not been able to do this. In practicing everyday virtues and exercising care in everyday speech, wherever he falls short, he dares not fail to exert himself; where he has more to offer, he dares not say it all. His words take account of his deeds, and his deeds take account of his words. How could the gentleman fail to be earnest and steadfast!

Benevolence is the secure dwelling of humankind; righteousness is its proper road.

Book of Changes

Kun is utterly yielding, yet firm in its movement; utterly still, yet square in its virtue.

By observing what endures, one can discern the true nature of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things.

This is what is meant by saying that the Changes contains four aspects of the way of the sages.

As a book, the Changes is vast and comprehensive, containing everything. Within it are the way of Heaven, the way of humankind, and the way of Earth. It brings together these Three Powers and doubles them, thus making six. These six are nothing other than the way of the Three Powers.

Await only righteousness [?; the opening transcription includes an illegible character]; government consists in nourishing the people.
Heaven alone is discerning and clear-sighted; the sage takes it as his model.
The Junior Preceptor, Junior Mentor, and Junior Guardian are called the Three Junior Dukes. They assist the Three Dukes in extending moral transformation, reverently aid Heaven and Earth, and assist me, the One Man.

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
褒灒神明
從征違期
造作過限
第叄場
策五道
問帝王肇興必有制作以化成天下我
聖祖高皇帝誕膺
天命驅逐胡元再造華夏經綸世道之制作可
得而悉數歟三代相繼皆有所因何我
===
聖祖之制作則盡革胡元之故歟其亦有所因
於古歟律令也禮制也
大誥也皆制作之大者也其綱領條目可槩舉
其數歟其合於先王之典者可各舉其
一二歟
列聖相繼纘集群書亦皆可以維持世道者歟

禮制
punctuated:
褒灒神明。
從征違期。
造作過限。

第叄場
策五道

問：帝王肇興，必有制作以化成天下。我聖祖高皇帝誕膺天命，驅逐胡元，再造華夏，經綸世道之制作，可得而悉數歟？三代相繼，皆有所因，何我聖祖之制作則盡革胡元之故歟？其亦有所因於古歟？律令也，禮制也，大誥也，皆制作之大者也，其綱領條目可槩舉其數歟？其合於先王之典者，可各舉其一二歟？列聖相繼，纘集群書，亦皆可以維持世道者歟？因事建立，每有條例。孝宗敬皇帝刪繁類聚，定爲成書，不知與律令、禮制
translation_en:
Commending divine efficacy [?].
Missing the appointed date for joining a military expedition.
Exceeding the deadline for construction or manufacture.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: When emperors and kings first rise, they invariably establish institutions to transform and bring order to all under Heaven. Our Sacred Progenitor, Emperor Gao, received Heaven’s mandate, expelled the Mongol Yuan, and restored the Chinese realm. Can the institutions he established to order the world be enumerated in full? The Three Dynasties succeeded one another, each retaining something from its predecessor. Why, then, did the institutions of our Sacred Progenitor entirely sweep away the old arrangements of the Mongol Yuan? Did they also draw upon antiquity? The statutes and ordinances, the ritual institutions, and the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) are all major instances of his institutional work. Can their guiding principles and detailed provisions be broadly enumerated? Can you give one or two examples from each of their accord with the canons of the former kings?

The successive sage emperors compiled numerous books: were these likewise all capable of sustaining order in the world? As arrangements were established in response to particular matters, regulations were repeatedly issued. Emperor Xiaozong Jing eliminated redundancies, grouped the material by category, and established a definitive compilation. We ask how it relates to the statutes and ordinances, the ritual institutions …

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
大誥之旨同歟異歟亦可相與並傳於萬世歟
孔子曰吾從周諸士子積學效用
國朝之制作不可不講也願明言以對
問氏生於三而師居其一焉說者謂經師
易得人師難得然經師人師亦有辨歟
學於荀卿者所習非不善也何以焚燒
其書學於秦相者非不惡也何以治爲
第一讓封於師與爲師起墳者孰優請
代師死與固言師寃者孰愈學於馬氏
===
者多矣孰爲賢於其師學於程氏者多
矣孰爲不失其正河汾之徒患斷曠肅
深寧簡正各有其人而可興禮樂者誰
歟湖蘇之徒淵篤純明直諒簡諒各有
其人而功業最著者誰歟韓昌黎一代
之山斗也而李習之皇甫湜未嘗以弟
子自列何歟歐陽公一代之宗師也而
曾子固蘇子瞻亦未嘗以師處之何歟
豈所謂人師者雖韓歐亦未足以當之
punctuated:
《大誥》之旨同歟，異歟？亦可相與並傳於萬世歟？孔子曰：「吾從周。」諸士子積學效用，國朝之制作不可不講也。願明言以對。
問：氏生於三，而師居其一焉。說者謂：「經師易得，人師難得。」然經師、人師亦有辨歟？學於荀卿者，所習非不善也，何以焚燒其書？學於秦相者，非不惡也，何以治爲第一？讓封於師與爲師起墳者孰優？請代師死與固言師寃者孰愈？學於馬氏者多矣，孰爲賢於其師？學於程氏者多矣，孰爲不失其正？河汾之徒，患斷、曠肅、深寧、簡正，各有其人，而可興禮樂者誰歟？湖蘇之徒，淵篤、純明、直諒、簡諒，各有其人，而功業最著者誰歟？韓昌黎，一代之山斗也，而李習之、皇甫湜未嘗以弟子自列，何歟？歐陽公，一代之宗師也，而曾子固、蘇子瞻亦未嘗以師處之，何歟？豈所謂人師者，雖韓、歐亦未足以當之
translation_en:
…and the purport of the Great Pronouncements: are they the same or different? Can these also be transmitted together for ten thousand generations? Confucius said, “I follow Zhou.” You candidates have accumulated learning with a view to putting it into service; you must therefore examine the institutions established by our dynasty. Please explain clearly in your answers.
Question: People [?] owe their lives to three sources, and the teacher is one of them. It is said, “A teacher of the classics is easy to find; a teacher who exemplifies human conduct is hard to find.” But is there a distinction between these two kinds of teacher? What the pupil of Xun Qing learned was certainly good; why, then, did he burn those books? The pupil of the chief minister of Qin studied under someone certainly wicked; why, then, was his administration ranked first? Of the man who yielded his enfeoffment to his teacher and the man who built a tomb for his teacher, which was superior? Of the man who asked to die in his teacher’s place and the man who steadfastly maintained that his teacher had been wronged, which was better? Many studied under Master Ma; who surpassed his teacher in worth? Many studied under Master Cheng; who preserved the correctness of his teaching? Among the disciples of the He–Fen school were men of anxious resolve [?], broad-minded solemnity, profound tranquillity, and unassuming rectitude; but who could revive rites and music? Among the disciples at Huzhou and Suzhou were men of profound sincerity, purity and discernment, uprightness and trustworthiness, and simplicity and good faith; but whose achievements were most outstanding? Han Changli was the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of his age; why, then, did Li Xizhi and Huangfu Shi never count themselves as his disciples? Lord Ouyang was a master of his age; why, then, did Zeng Zigu and Su Zizhan likewise never treat him as their teacher? Could it be that even Han and Ouyang were insufficiently qualified to be what is called a teacher who exemplifies human conduct …

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
歟願相與講之以知古之爲師弟子賢
否
問備敵禦侮撥亂反正不能不假乎兵然
用兵有道而亦有法焉非茍焉以徒設
也故王以衆謝以寡郭以寬李以嚴而
咸以能兵名是豈無法而亦豈無道哉
傳曰陷之死地而後生置之亡地而後
存是以當時之用兵者或濟河焚舟勝
或背水囊沙勝或以繩兵勝或以火兵
===
勝焉又曰天時不如地利地利不如人
和是以當時之用兵者或以失井陘敗
或以得下陽勝或以失關中之民敗或
以得漢中之民勝若果必置之亡地死
地而後可以取勝耶則地利不必恃人
和不必倚矣果必本之地利人和而後
可以制勝耶則亡地不當據死地不當
扼矣然則孫武孟子之説果矛盾而不
相通歟抑可並行而不悖歟是必有至
punctuated:
歟？願相與講之，以知古之爲師弟子賢否。

問：備敵禦侮，撥亂反正，不能不假乎兵。然用兵有道，而亦有法焉，非茍焉以徒設也。故王以衆，謝以寡，郭以寬，李以嚴，而咸以能兵名，是豈無法，而亦豈無道哉？傳曰：「陷之死地而後生，置之亡地而後存。」是以當時之用兵者，或濟河焚舟勝，或背水囊沙勝，或以繩兵勝，或以火兵勝焉。又曰：「天時不如地利，地利不如人和。」是以當時之用兵者，或以失井陘敗，或以得下陽勝，或以失關中之民敗，或以得漢中之民勝。若果必置之亡地死地而後可以取勝耶，則地利不必恃，人和不必倚矣。果必本之地利人和而後可以制勝耶，則亡地不當據，死地不當扼矣。然則孫武、孟子之説果矛盾而不相通歟？抑可並行而不悖歟？是必有至
translation_en:
…? I hope that we may discuss this together, to understand whether those who served as teachers and disciples in antiquity were worthy or unworthy.

Question: Preparing against enemies, resisting aggression, putting down disorder, and restoring proper order inevitably require recourse to armed force. Yet employing troops involves both guiding principles and practical methods; these are not casually devised to serve no purpose. Thus Wang employed large forces, Xie small ones, Guo leniency, and Li strictness, yet all won renown for military skill. Could they have lacked methods, or indeed guiding principles? A transmitted text says: “Plunge them into deadly ground, and only then will they live; place them on ground of destruction, and only then will they survive.” Accordingly, commanders of those times sometimes won by crossing a river and burning their boats, sometimes by fighting with their backs to a river or using sacks of sand, sometimes by using ropes in warfare [?], and sometimes by using fire in warfare.

It is also said: “Favorable timing granted by Heaven is less important than advantageous terrain; advantageous terrain is less important than harmony among the people.” Accordingly, commanders of those times sometimes suffered defeat through losing Jingxing, sometimes won through taking Xiayang, sometimes suffered defeat through losing the allegiance of the people of Guanzhong, and sometimes won through gaining the allegiance of the people of Hanzhong. If troops must indeed be placed on ground of destruction and death before victory can be won, then there is no need to rely on advantageous terrain or harmony among the people. If victory must indeed rest upon advantageous terrain and harmony among the people, then one ought not occupy ground of destruction or hold deadly ground. Are the teachings of Sun Wu and Mengzi, then, truly contradictory and irreconcilable? Or can both be practiced without conflict? There must surely be a supremely…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
當一定之論蜀地用兵今方持勝諸士
子經心屬目籌之者熟矣試言之以觀
文事武備之用其毋曰我未之學也
問盜賊竊發雖盛世不能無然或有之而
欲平定安輯剿撫二者之外無他術也
稽古驗今不能無疑焉撫事姑息若不
可恃也然守渤海而盜皆解散守泰山
而賊帥先歸廣陵之賊悉面縛以投欵
清河之盜悉相率以出降專事征剿果
===
可恃乎剿必血刃若所不忍也然在廣
漢而平賊萬人在琅邪而獲賊萬級除
徐州之驕卒數千夷幇源洞之叛寇七
萬專事縱釋果可再乎邇者各處鼠竊
群起
朝廷命將出師已平定十之八九矣其餘黨
孽尚延殘喘於谿谷之中撫則有復叛
之虞剿則有弗盡之慮果何術以收萬
全之功抑或別有所本歟諸士子學古
punctuated:
當一定之論。蜀地用兵，今方持勝，諸士子經心屬目，籌之者熟矣。試言之，以觀文事武備之用，其毋曰我未之學也。

問：盜賊竊發，雖盛世不能無。然或有之，而欲平定安輯，剿撫二者之外，無他術也。稽古驗今，不能無疑焉。撫事姑息，若不可恃也；然守渤海而盜皆解散，守泰山而賊帥先歸，廣陵之賊悉面縛以投欵，清河之盜悉相率以出降，專事征剿果可恃乎？剿必血刃，若所不忍也；然在廣漢而平賊萬人，在琅邪而獲賊萬級，除徐州之驕卒數千，夷幇源洞之叛寇七萬，專事縱釋果可再乎？邇者各處鼠竊群起，朝廷命將出師，已平定十之八九矣。其餘黨孽尚延殘喘於谿谷之中，撫則有復叛之虞，剿則有弗盡之慮，果何術以收萬全之功？抑或別有所本歟？諸士子學古
translation_en:
…a sound and definitive judgment. Military operations in Shu are now maintaining the advantage. You candidates have devoted your attention to this matter and considered it thoroughly. Explain your views, so that we may observe how you apply civil learning and military preparedness. Do not say, “I have not studied this.”

Question: Even in a flourishing age, outbreaks of banditry cannot be entirely avoided. When they occur, however, there are no means of suppressing disorder and restoring peace beyond military suppression and conciliation. Yet examining antiquity and testing it against the present inevitably raises doubts. Conciliation involves indulgence and seems unreliable. Nevertheless, under one governor of Bohai the bandits all dispersed; under one governor of Taishan the rebel leaders were the first to submit. The bandits of Guangling all presented themselves with their hands bound behind their backs in token of submission, and the bandits of Qinghe all followed one another out to surrender. Can exclusive reliance on punitive campaigns and suppression truly be trusted?

Suppression inevitably bloodies the blade and seems unbearable. Yet in Guanghan ten thousand rebels were subdued; in Langye ten thousand rebel heads were taken; several thousand unruly soldiers in Xuzhou were eliminated; and seventy thousand rebels at Bangyuan Cave were destroyed. Can a policy devoted solely to releasing offenders really be repeated?

Recently, bands of petty thieves have sprung up everywhere. The court appointed commanders and dispatched armies, and eight or nine out of ten have already been pacified. Their remaining adherents and rebellious remnants still cling to life in the ravines and valleys. Conciliation carries the danger that they will rebel again; suppression raises the concern that they cannot be eliminated entirely. By what means, then, can complete success be achieved? Or is there some other foundation on which it depends? You candidates study antiquity…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
入官於前代已然之迹今日當爲之事
必講之熟矣其爲我明著其說以俟採
焉
問蜀之富饒著自古昔迨入
國朝休養既久生齒日繁奈何俗漸侈肆釁
蘗潛萌䵷黽之孽聚既興鴻鴈之哀鳴
遂切今盜賊雖漸次輯弭而地方之殘
疲已甚賑恤撫安所當急也
朝廷嘗出
===
內帑以濟不足
也嘗降優
恩至渥矣柰所出有限顛連無窮似未能徧濟
詔以免租稅
意亦切矣柰邊方告急軍儲空乏似未容盡免
也時在當道者聞嘗禁差役以省民力
也然反側未安餘蘖未滅差役果能槩
免乎又嘗禁科取以節民財也然戍守
仰給供億紛紜科取果能悉已乎議者
punctuated:
入官，於前代已然之迹、今日當爲之事，必講之熟矣。其爲我明著其說，以俟採焉。

問：蜀之富饒，著自古昔。迨入國朝，休養既久，生齒日繁。奈何俗漸侈肆，釁蘗潛萌，䵷黽之孽聚既興，鴻鴈之哀鳴遂切。今盜賊雖漸次輯弭，而地方之殘疲已甚，賑恤撫安所當急也。朝廷嘗出內帑以濟不足也，嘗降優恩，至渥矣。柰所出有限，顛連無窮，似未能徧濟。詔以免租稅，意亦切矣。柰邊方告急，軍儲空乏，似未容盡免也。時在當道者，聞嘗禁差役以省民力也。然反側未安，餘蘖未滅，差役果能槩免乎？又嘗禁科取以節民財也。然戍守仰給，供億紛紜，科取果能悉已乎？議者
translation_en:
…and enter official service, you must surely have thoroughly studied the precedents of earlier dynasties and the measures that ought to be undertaken today. Set out your views clearly for me, so that they may be considered for adoption.

Question: Shu’s wealth and abundance have been renowned since antiquity. Under our dynasty, a long period of recuperation has brought daily growth in its population. How, then, have customs gradually become extravagant and unrestrained, while the seeds of disorder have secretly sprouted? Once villainous gatherings of “frogs and toads” arose, the plaintive cries of the “wild geese”—the suffering people—became acute. Although the bandits are now gradually being pacified, the region is already gravely ravaged and exhausted. Relief, assistance, and the restoration of peace are urgent tasks.

The court has disbursed funds from the Palace Treasury to make up deficiencies and has bestowed exceedingly generous favors. Yet the funds disbursed are limited, while distress is boundless; it seems impossible to provide relief to everyone. Its edict remitting taxes likewise expresses an earnest intention. Yet emergencies are reported on the frontier, and military stores are depleted; it seems impossible to remit everything.

We hear that those currently in authority have prohibited service requisitions to conserve the people’s strength. Yet the disaffected remain unsettled, and the remnants of rebellion have not been eliminated. Can service obligations really be waived across the board? They have also prohibited levies to conserve the people’s resources. Yet the garrisons depend on these supplies, and provisioning demands are manifold. Can such levies really all be stopped? Those discussing the matter…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
又謂有治人無治法法苟得其人法無不
行而地方之殘疲可救矣然今有事於
蜀之官上者極一時之選固無容議次
者果能盡得其人乎茲欲使顛連得所
而賑恤不煩於奏
請租稅可免而邊儲不至於缺乏防守有備而
差役不勞乎民供億有賴而科取不及
乎下又欲使官皆得人而救時之法以
行上下相安而富饒之俗可復是必有
===
道焉諸士子積學有年矧生茲土諒講
之熟矣願明言以對將以
獻於
朝廷而行之毋諉曰思不出其位
punctuated: 又謂有治人，無治法，法苟得其人，法無不行，而地方之殘疲可救矣。然今有事於蜀之官，上者極一時之選，固無容議；次者果能盡得其人乎？茲欲使顛連得所，而賑恤不煩於奏請；租稅可免，而邊儲不至於缺乏；防守有備，而差役不勞乎民；供億有賴，而科取不及乎下。又欲使官皆得人，而救時之法以行；上下相安，而富饒之俗可復，是必有道焉。諸士子積學有年，矧生茲土，諒講之熟矣。願明言以對，將以獻於朝廷而行之，毋諉曰思不出其位。
translation_en:
… further maintain that there are men who bring about good government, but no laws that do so of themselves. If the right men are found to administer the laws, no law will fail to be implemented, and the devastation and exhaustion of the region can be remedied. Yet among the officials now serving in Shu, those at the highest level are the finest choices of the age and certainly beyond question; but at the next level, can all the appointments truly have gone to the right men?

We now wish to ensure that those in distress find relief, without requiring repeated memorials requesting authorization for aid; that taxes can be remitted without leaving frontier stores deficient; that defensive preparations are adequate without exhausting the people through service obligations; and that supplies are assured without imposing exactions upon the populace. We also wish every office to be filled by the right man, so that measures to remedy the troubles of the times can be implemented, and those above and below to live in mutual peace, so that the former conditions of prosperity may be restored. There must be a way to accomplish this.

You examination candidates have devoted years to learning; moreover, you were born in this land and surely have discussed these matters thoroughly. Please set forth your answers clearly, so that they may be submitted to the imperial court and put into practice. Do not evade the task by saying, “One’s thoughts do not extend beyond one’s official position.”

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
立不中門行不履閾
毛萬
同考試官學正鄭　批〔揭書出題不意窘筆惟此作繪簡為文紆徐蔚茂且達盡夫子敬君之意家數〕
〔不同錄之以冠他作〕
同考試官學正魏　批〔文字機軸關鍵與衆作〕
〔自是遠甚分明聖人立行之軌度也敬服敬服〕
===
考試官教諭立　批〔盛德之容模寫宛然〕
考試官教授陳　批〔體貼最是〕
門人記聖人之在朝而止趨皆存乎敬焉蓋聖
人之敬無往而不存也矧其在朝而一止一趨
豈有不敬者哉昔門人記聖人在朝之容意謂
吾夫子之聖也道無往而不在敬無時而不存
彼鳴玉而朝待漏而止臣未見君當立於門也
然棖闑之間乃人君出入之處焉夫子之立於
公門清光固未仰接而氷心先已夔夔待茬振
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
立不中門，行不履閾。
毛萬

同考試官學正鄭批〔揭書出題，不意窘筆，惟此作繪簡為文，紆徐蔚茂，且達盡夫子敬君之意，家數〕〔不同，錄之以冠他作。〕
同考試官學正魏批〔文字機軸關鍵，與衆作〕〔自是遠甚，分明聖人立行之軌度也。敬服！敬服！〕
考試官教諭立批〔盛德之容，模寫宛然。〕
考試官教授陳批〔體貼最是。〕

門人記聖人之在朝，而止趨皆存乎敬焉。蓋聖人之敬，無往而不存也。矧其在朝，而一止一趨，豈有不敬者哉？昔門人記聖人在朝之容，意謂吾夫子之聖也，道無往而不在，敬無時而不存。彼鳴玉而朝，待漏而止，臣未見君，當立於門也。然棖闑之間，乃人君出入之處焉。夫子之立於公門，清光固未仰接，而氷心先已夔夔，待茬振
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“When standing, he did not occupy the center of the gateway; when walking, he did not tread on the threshold.”
Mao Wan

Associate Examiner Zheng, School Instructor, comments: “Drawing a topic from the book unexpectedly puts the writer’s brush in difficulty. This composition alone turns the simple passage into a vivid essay [?], leisurely and richly developed; moreover, it fully conveys the Master’s reverence for his ruler. Its approach is distinctive, so we record it here at the head of the other compositions.”

Associate Examiner Wei, School Instructor, comments: “The organizing conception and crucial articulations of this essay are far removed indeed from those of the other compositions. It clearly presents the standards governing the sage’s standing and walking. Admirable! Admirable!”

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The demeanor of one endowed with abundant virtue is vividly portrayed.”

Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “Its sympathetic understanding is most exact.”

The disciples recorded that, when the sage was at court, reverence informed both his stopping and his advancing. For the sage’s reverence was present wherever he went. How much more so when he was at court: could any instance of stopping or advancing have lacked reverence? When the disciples of old recorded the sage’s demeanor at court, their meaning was this: such was our Master’s sageliness that the Way was present wherever he went, and reverence was present at every moment. Going to court with his jade pendants chiming, he paused to await the appointed hour marked by the water clock. Before a minister had seen his ruler, he was to stand at the gateway. Yet the space between the side posts and the central post was where the ruler entered and departed. When the Master stood at the palace gateway, although he had not yet looked up to receive the ruler’s radiant presence, his heart, pure as ice, was already reverent and apprehensive, awaiting [?]…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
之言而不得親聆其謦欬千載之下不勝景仰
也噫
居子之道四丘未能一焉所求乎子以事
父未能也所求乎臣以事君未能也所
求乎弟以事兄未能也所求乎朋友先
施之未能也庸德之行庸言之謹有所
不足不敢不勉有餘不敢盡言顧行行
顧言君子胡不慥慥爾
楊恂
同試官訓導王　批〔題本明白但諸作謂聖　自責自脩以求盡君子之道至贊美處則不通矣此〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔見理精切出辭簡健蓋　卷體認真切非用心之精者不能與此宜錄以示式〕
考試官教諭丘　批〔得長題家數　嘗究心於君子之道者〕
考試官教授陳　批〔該括得盡〕
===
聖人不自居君子之道必詳其道而美之也蓋
君子之道聖人之能事也今焉謙不自居而又
punctuated:
之言，而不得親聆其謦欬，千載之下，不勝景仰也。噫！

居子之道四，丘未能一焉：所求乎子，以事父，未能也；所求乎臣，以事君，未能也；所求乎弟，以事兄，未能也；所求乎朋友，先施之，未能也。庸德之行，庸言之謹，有所不足，不敢不勉；有餘，不敢盡。言顧行，行顧言，君子胡不慥慥爾！

楊恂

同試官訓導王　批〔題本明白，但諸作謂聖　自責自脩，以求盡君子之道，至贊美處則不通矣。此〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔見理精切，出辭簡健，蓋　卷體認真切，非用心之精者不能與此，宜錄以示式。〕
考試官教諭丘　批〔得長題家數　嘗究心於君子之道者〕
考試官教授陳　批〔該括得盡〕

聖人不自居君子之道，必詳其道而美之也。蓋君子之道，聖人之能事也。今焉謙不自居，而又
translation_en:
…his words, yet unable to hear his voice in person, we who live a thousand years later cannot contain our reverent admiration. Ah!

“There are four aspects to the way of the gentleman [?]; I, Qiu, have not been able to fulfill even one. To serve my father as I would require a son to serve me—I have not been able to do this. To serve my ruler as I would require a minister to serve me—I have not been able to do this. To serve my elder brother as I would require a younger brother to serve me—I have not been able to do this. To take the initiative in treating friends as I would require them to treat me—I have not been able to do this. In practicing ordinary virtues and exercising care in ordinary speech, wherever he falls short, he dares not fail to exert himself; where he has something to spare, he dares not say everything. His words take account of his conduct, and his conduct takes account of his words. How could the gentleman fail to be earnest and sincere!”

Yang Xun.

Associate Examiner [?] Wang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The topic itself is clear. But the various essays say that the sage [?] reproaches and cultivates himself in order to fulfill the way of the gentleman completely; when they reach the passage of praise, however, this interpretation makes no sense. This… [?]〕
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔His understanding of principle is precise and incisive, and his language concise and vigorous. Indeed [?], this paper shows a genuine and penetrating grasp; no one lacking refinement of thought could attain this. It should be recorded as a model.〕
Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: 〔He has mastered the techniques for handling a long topic. [He is] someone who has devoted thought to the way of the gentleman. [?]〕
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: 〔It encompasses everything fully.〕

The sage does not claim for himself attainment of the way of the gentleman, but necessarily sets forth that way in detail and praises it. For the way of the gentleman is what the sage is fully capable of accomplishing. Here, however, he humbly declines to claim it for himself, and furthermore…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
之東則依棖少立容或在闑之右也不敢當棖
闑之中焉時在棖之西則拂棖少佇亦或在闑
之右也不敢居棖闑之間焉是豈矯揉而然邪
蓋立中門則當尊夫子之心敬君之至也豈敢
當尊也哉承召而入奉命而出出入公門必過
閾也然門限內外乃人君臨御之所焉夫子時
過於公門君顏雖未仰瞻而亦心先已慄慄鞠
躬而入繩趨尺步之有節足雖踧踖舉動從容
不敢加足於門限之上也下堦而出循規蹈矩
===
之有常足雖踧踖步履安詳不敢置足於門下
之閾也是豈強勉而然哉蓋行履閾則不恪夫
子敬君無時而不然也豈有不恪也哉吁一立
一行當敬而敬入門過門易忽不忽自非盛德
之至烏能動容周旋中禮如此哉大抵鄉黨一
書門弟子記夫子之行實也他如宗廟朝廷事
上接下之禮衣服飲食之節擯相交友之誠無
一不載之詳今讀其書考其事究然如聖人之
在目也杏壇迹蕪木鐸聲微徒聞盡出箇聖人
punctuated: 之東，則依棖少立，容或在闑之右也，不敢當棖闑之中焉。時在棖之西，則拂棖少佇，亦或在闑之右也，不敢居棖闑之間焉。是豈矯揉而然邪？蓋立中門則當尊，夫子之心，敬君之至也，豈敢當尊也哉？承召而入，奉命而出，出入公門必過閾也。然門限內外，乃人君臨御之所焉。夫子時過於公門，君顏雖未仰瞻，而亦心先已慄慄。鞠躬而入，繩趨尺步之有節，足雖踧踖，舉動從容，不敢加足於門限之上也。下堦而出，循規蹈矩之有常，足雖踧踖，步履安詳，不敢置足於門下之閾也。是豈強勉而然哉？蓋行履閾則不恪，夫子敬君，無時而不然也，豈有不恪也哉？吁！一立一行，當敬而敬；入門過門，易忽不忽。自非盛德之至，烏能動容周旋中禮如此哉？大抵《鄉黨》一書，門弟子記夫子之行實也。他如宗廟朝廷事上接下之禮，衣服飲食之節，擯相交友之誠，無一不載之詳。今讀其書，考其事，究然如聖人之在目也。杏壇迹蕪，木鐸聲微，徒聞盡出箇聖人
translation_en:
…to its east, he would stand briefly beside the doorjamb, perhaps to the right of the central doorpost, not daring to occupy the middle of the space between jamb and central post. When to the west of the jamb, he would pause briefly close against it, likewise perhaps to the right of the central post, not daring to take his place between jamb and central post. Could this have resulted from affected or contrived behavior? To stand in the middle of the gateway was to occupy the position of honor. The Master's heart was utterly reverent toward his ruler: how could he dare occupy that position?

He entered when summoned and departed at his ruler's command; entering or leaving the palace gate necessarily meant passing over its threshold. Yet the area both inside and outside that threshold was where the ruler presided. Whenever the Master passed through the palace gate, even before looking up to behold his ruler's countenance, his heart was already trembling with awe. He entered with his body bowed, his straight course and measured steps governed by proper rhythm. Though his feet moved with apprehensive care, his movements were composed, and he did not dare set foot upon the threshold. Descending the steps to leave, he consistently observed the prescribed forms. Though his feet moved with apprehensive care, his steps were calm and unhurried, and he did not dare place his foot upon the threshold beneath the gate. Could this have resulted from forcing himself to act so? To tread upon the threshold was irreverent. The Master revered his ruler at every moment: how could there be any irreverence?

Ah! In every act of standing or walking, he showed reverence wherever reverence was due. In entering and passing through gateways, where others might easily become heedless, he was never heedless. Without virtue perfected to the highest degree, how could every movement and turn of his body accord with ritual in this way? Broadly speaking, the text “Village Life” (Xiangdang) records the Master's actual conduct as set down by his disciples. Other matters, such as the rites for serving superiors and dealing with subordinates in ancestral temples and at court, the rules governing clothing, food, and drink, and the sincerity shown in receiving guests, assisting at ceremonies, and associating with friends—all are recorded in detail. Reading this text today and examining these deeds, one has the vivid impression [?] that the sage stands before one's eyes. The traces of the Apricot Platform are overgrown, and the sound of the wooden-clapper bell has grown faint; one merely hears a whole sage brought forth [?]…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
詳其道以美之其道不遠人爲道不遠之意於
此亦可見哉中庸論道之費隱至此引夫子之
言謂夫君子之道其目有四而求之在我未能
其一葢孝以事親子之道也責子以孝而我之
孝親者恐未純忠以事君臣之道也責臣以忠
而我之忠君者恐未盡責弟之恭於吾吾亦有
兄也未能篤厚夫天倫責朋友之信於我我亦
朋友也未能先施其不欺君子自責如此於是
以子臣弟友之道體諸身確乎踐履之皆實孝
===
弟忠信之理宣諸聲鑿乎防檢之擇可力行難
常患於不足知其不足而不敢不勉則行益力
矣放言易常失之有餘知其有餘而不敢少放
則謹益至矣謹之至則言爲有物而言能顧行
行之力則行爲有常而行能顧言君子言行相
顧如此則是道充於内而無不足體於身而無
不盡豈不慥慥篤實矣乎天自責之中而寓自
脩之理自脩其理因見自責之實君子之道蓋
如此此我之所未能也中庸引之以明道之費
punctuated:
詳其道以美之，其道不遠人，爲道不遠之意，於此亦可見哉！

中庸論道之費隱，至此引夫子之言，謂夫君子之道，其目有四，而求之在我，未能其一。葢孝以事親，子之道也；責子以孝，而我之孝親者恐未純。忠以事君，臣之道也；責臣以忠，而我之忠君者恐未盡。責弟之恭於吾，吾亦有兄也，未能篤厚夫天倫；責朋友之信於我，我亦朋友也，未能先施其不欺。君子自責如此，於是以子臣弟友之道體諸身，確乎踐履之皆實；孝弟忠信之理宣諸聲，鑿乎防檢之擇可。力行難，常患於不足，知其不足而不敢不勉，則行益力矣；放言易，常失之有餘，知其有餘而不敢少放，則謹益至矣。謹之至，則言爲有物，而言能顧行；行之力，則行爲有常，而行能顧言。君子言行相顧如此，則是道充於内而無不足，體於身而無不盡，豈不慥慥篤實矣乎！天自責之中而寓自脩之理，自脩其理，因見自責之實。君子之道蓋如此，此我之所未能也。中庸引之以明道之費
translation_en:
…expound his Way in detail to praise him. His Way is not remote from people: can we not also see here the meaning of pursuing the Way without departing from what is close at hand?

In discussing the Way’s extensive reach and hidden subtlety, the Doctrine of the Mean here quotes the Master’s words: the way of the gentleman has four aspects, yet, examining himself, he finds that he has not achieved even one. To serve one’s parents with filial devotion is the way of a son. Yet, while demanding filial devotion from his son, he fears that his own devotion to his parents is not pure. To serve one’s ruler with loyalty is the way of a minister. Yet, while demanding loyalty from his ministers, he fears that his own loyalty to his ruler is not complete. He demands respect toward himself from his younger brother, yet he too has an elder brother, and has not fully strengthened this natural familial bond. He demands trustworthiness toward himself from his friends, yet he too is a friend, and has not first shown them that he will not deceive them. Such is the gentleman’s scrutiny of himself. Accordingly, he embodies in his own person the ways of son, minister, younger brother, and friend, firmly making every act of practice genuine. He gives voice to the principles of filial devotion, brotherly respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness, rigorously restraining and examining himself to choose what is acceptable [?].

Vigorous practice is difficult, and one is constantly troubled by falling short. Knowing that he falls short, he dares not fail to exert himself, and thus his practice becomes more vigorous. Unrestrained speech is easy, and one constantly errs by saying too much. Knowing that he says too much, he dares not allow himself even a little license, and thus his caution becomes still more complete. When caution is complete, his words have substance, and his words take account of his conduct. When practice is vigorous, his conduct has constancy, and his conduct takes account of his words. When the gentleman’s words and conduct take account of one another in this way, the Way fills him inwardly without deficiency and is embodied in his person without anything left unrealized. Is this not earnest and substantial sincerity?

Within self-reproach lies the principle of self-cultivation [?]; through cultivating that principle in oneself, the sincerity of one’s self-reproach becomes apparent. Such, indeed, is the way of the gentleman: ‘This is what I have not yet achieved.’ The Doctrine of the Mean quotes this to illuminate the Way’s extensive reach…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
隱其意切哉大抵道者率性而已本不遠於人
也但人之爲道自遠耳子思論道之費隱而詳
引聖人之言曰治己治人曰愛己愛人至此又
以責人責己以爲言誘啓後人無非欲其不遠
人以爲道也道其不明人趨異端子思喫緊爲
人憂之深故其言之切慮之遠故其說之詳也
詳學者須要識得
仁人之安宅也義人之正路也
張芊
同考試官教諭吴　批〔安宅正路處親切有味且結出孟子立言之意非素〕〔學仁義任斯道以扶世者不足以與此〕
同考試官教諭張　批〔發明仁義之旨通篇明甚執此可以占子所居所由之不苟矣〕
考試官教諭丘　批〔典實可取〕
考試官撿陳　批〔說理明白〕
大賢論理有爲人所當居者有爲人所當由者
蓋仁義之理乃吾性之固有而可居可由也大
punctuated:
隱，其意切哉！大抵道者，率性而已，本不遠於人也，但人之爲道自遠耳。子思論道之費隱，而詳引聖人之言，曰治己治人，曰愛己愛人，至此又以責人責己以爲言，誘啓後人，無非欲其不遠人以爲道也。道其不明，人趨異端。子思喫緊爲人，憂之深，故其言之切；慮之遠，故其說之詳也。詳學者須要識得。

仁，人之安宅也；義，人之正路也。
張芊

同考試官教諭吴，批〔安宅正路處親切有味且結出孟子立言之意非素〕〔學仁義任斯道以扶世者不足以與此〕。
同考試官教諭張，批〔發明仁義之旨通篇明甚執此可以占子所居所由之不苟矣〕。
考試官教諭丘，批〔典實可取〕。
考試官撿陳，批〔說理明白〕。

大賢論理，有爲人所當居者，有爲人所當由者。蓋仁義之理，乃吾性之固有，而可居可由也。大
translation_en:
…and hiddenness: how earnest his meaning is! Broadly speaking, the Way consists simply in following one’s nature; it is inherently not far from human beings. It is only people themselves who, in pursuing the Way, make it remote. Zisi discusses the Way’s all-pervasiveness and hiddenness, quoting the sage’s words at length: governing oneself and governing others, loving oneself and loving others. Here he also speaks of holding others and oneself accountable. In guiding and enlightening later generations, his sole purpose is that they should not depart from human beings in pursuing the Way. When the Way is not understood, people turn toward heterodox teachings. Zisi was deeply concerned for others: because his concern was profound, his words were earnest; because his foresight reached far, his explanations were detailed. Students must grasp this [the preceding 詳 is unclear].

“Benevolence is the secure dwelling of human beings; righteousness is their proper road.”
By Zhang Qian.

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “The passages on the secure dwelling and proper road are apt and rich in meaning. Moreover, the conclusion brings out Mencius’s intention in making this statement. Someone who had not long studied benevolence and righteousness and taken responsibility for this Way in order to sustain the world would not be capable of this.”

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of benevolence and righteousness is elucidated with great clarity throughout. From this one may judge that you are scrupulous about where you dwell and the road you follow.”

Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: “Grounded in the classics and substantial; worthy of approval.”

Examiner Chen, whose title is transcribed as 撿 [?], comments: “Explains the principles clearly.”

In discussing principle, the great worthy distinguishes that in which people ought to dwell from that along which they ought to proceed. For the principles of benevolence and righteousness are inherent in our nature: they provide a dwelling and a path to follow. The great…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
賢析而言之以見人當常體之也歟想其意謂
夫理寓于人而人具乎理仁也者乃人固有之
理也一德渾全而重厚不遷有天理自然之安
群邪退聽而純全不雜無人欲陷溺之危雖不
峻宇之軒昂而居之者安處之者豫可以優游
而卒歲雖非廣廈之帡幪而宅之無危舍之無
懼可以俯仰而終身恢宏不陋經久無虞誠爲
人之安宅也仁爲安宅人可不常居於是也乎
義也者亦人本然之性也酬酢萬變而事無不
===
宜乃天理之當行裁制百爲而施無不當無人
欲之邪曲雖非周道之平平而義理之坦途天
下共由古今通行也誰能外之而他適雖非康
莊之蕩蕩而義理之大道出入必由往來必行
也孰能外之而他從至當不易無黨無偏誠爲
人之正路也義爲正路人可不恒由於是也乎
吁理切于人如此而人自不察豈不爲自暴自
棄哉大抵戰國之時人心陷溺居者以數仞爲
安宅行者以詭遇爲正路不知仁義爲何等物
punctuated:
賢析而言之，以見人當常體之也歟？想其意謂：夫理寓于人，而人具乎理。仁也者，乃人固有之理也。一德渾全，而重厚不遷，有天理自然之安；群邪退聽，而純全不雜，無人欲陷溺之危。雖不峻宇之軒昂，而居之者安，處之者豫，可以優游而卒歲；雖非廣廈之帡幪，而宅之無危，舍之無懼，可以俯仰而終身。恢宏不陋，經久無虞，誠爲人之安宅也。仁爲安宅，人可不常居於是也乎？

義也者，亦人本然之性也。酬酢萬變，而事無不宜，乃天理之當行；裁制百爲，而施無不當，無人欲之邪曲。雖非周道之平平，而義理之坦途，天下共由，古今通行也，誰能外之而他適？雖非康莊之蕩蕩，而義理之大道，出入必由，往來必行也，孰能外之而他從？至當不易，無黨無偏，誠爲人之正路也。義爲正路，人可不恒由於是也乎？

吁！理切于人如此，而人自不察，豈不爲自暴自棄哉？大抵戰國之時，人心陷溺，居者以數仞爲安宅，行者以詭遇爲正路，不知仁義爲何等物
translation_en:
…the great worthy discusses them separately to show that people should constantly embody them, does he not? His meaning, we may suppose, is this: Principle resides in human beings, and human beings possess principle. Benevolence is the principle inherently possessed by human beings. Its single virtue is whole and complete, substantial and steadfast, possessing the natural security of Heaven’s principle. All evils withdraw before it; pure and entire, it is unmixed, free from the danger of being engulfed by human desires. Though it lacks the lofty grandeur of a towering house, those who dwell in it are secure and those who abide in it are at ease, able to pass their years in untroubled contentment. Though it offers no shelter like a spacious mansion, those who make it their home face no danger, and those who lodge in it know no fear, able to spend their whole lives at ease. Expansive rather than cramped, enduring without cause for anxiety, it truly is humanity’s secure dwelling. Since benevolence is the secure dwelling, can people fail to dwell constantly within it?

Righteousness, too, is humanity’s original nature. Responding to countless changes, it leaves no affair unfittingly handled: it is Heaven’s principle as it ought to be put into practice. Regulating every action, it leaves no application inappropriate, free from the perversity of human desires. Though it is no level highway, the smooth path of righteousness and principle is followed by all under Heaven and traversed alike in antiquity and the present. Who could depart from it and go elsewhere? Though it is no broad thoroughfare, the great road of righteousness and principle must be followed whenever one goes out or comes in, and traveled whenever one comes or goes. Who could leave it and follow another course? Supremely fitting and unchanging, without partiality or bias, it truly is humanity’s correct road. Since righteousness is the correct road, can people fail to follow it constantly?

Alas! Principle bears so directly upon human beings, yet they themselves fail to perceive it. Is this not to injure and abandon themselves? In the Warring States period, broadly speaking, people’s hearts were engulfed in desire. In choosing where to dwell, they regarded houses several ren high as secure dwellings; in choosing how to act, they regarded devious expedients as the correct road. They did not know what benevolence and righteousness were…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
也孟子生丁是時哀其暴棄借安宅以明其仁
假正路以明其義使人知所居非所安所由非
其正其可居可由者在此而不在彼也噫七篇
之中無非此意扶世立教之功豈小小哉
易
坤至柔而動也剛至靜而德方
楊恂
同考試官訓導王　批〔坤卦一題講柔剛靜方〕〔處人多紕謬子能剗腐撰新不數言而寫盡坤貞之妙〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔文言釋坤貞之義此篇〕〔發明殆盡不意詹𢘽之下而有是作真妙於文哉〕
蘊讀之令人神爽其可敬也夫
===
考試官教諭丘　批〔得坤貞之旨〕
考試官教授陳　批〔說理之文自別〕
文言申坤貞之義體妙於無爲用顯於有爲蓋
體之無爲者順也用之有爲者健也順而且健
此坤所以利牝馬之貞歟文言申明其旨至矣
昔吾夫子傳彖既以地道明坤義而文言又申
punctuated:
也。孟子生丁是時，哀其暴棄，借安宅以明其仁，假正路以明其義，使人知所居非所安，所由非其正，其可居可由者在此而不在彼也。噫！七篇之中，無非此意。扶世立教之功，豈小小哉！

易
坤至柔而動也剛，至靜而德方。
楊恂

同考試官訓導王批〔坤卦一題，講柔剛靜方〕〔處，人多紕謬。子能剗腐撰新，不數言而寫盡坤貞之妙。〕
同考試官教諭李批〔文言釋坤貞之義，此篇〕〔發明殆盡。不意詹𢘽之下而有是作，真妙於文哉！〕
蘊讀之，令人神爽，其可敬也夫！

考試官教諭丘批〔得坤貞之旨。〕
考試官教授陳批〔說理之文自別。〕

《文言》申坤貞之義，體妙於無爲，用顯於有爲。蓋體之無爲者，順也；用之有爲者，健也。順而且健，此坤所以利牝馬之貞歟！《文言》申明其旨至矣！昔吾夫子傳彖，既以地道明坤義，而《文言》又申
translation_en:
…Mencius lived in precisely such a time. Grieving over people's self-destruction and self-abandonment, he used the image of a secure dwelling to elucidate benevolence, and that of the proper road to elucidate righteousness. He thereby enabled people to understand that where they dwelt was no place of security, and that the road they followed was not the proper one: what they should inhabit and follow lay here, not there. Ah! Throughout the seven books of the Mencius, this intention is everywhere present. Could his achievement in sustaining the world and establishing moral instruction be called trifling?

Book of Changes
“Kun is utterly yielding, yet firm in its movement; utterly still, yet square in its virtue.”
Yang Xun

Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “On this topic concerning the hexagram Kun, many people make errors when explaining yieldingness, firmness, stillness, and squareness. You have cleared away stale formulations and composed something fresh, fully conveying the subtlety of Kun's constancy in just a few words.”
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) explains the meaning of Kun's constancy. This essay elucidates it almost exhaustively. I had not expected such a composition under ‘zhan yi’ [?]. Truly masterful writing!”
“Yun [?]: Reading it refreshes the spirit. How worthy of respect!”

Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: “It captures the essential meaning of Kun's constancy.”
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “Writing that explains principle is in a class of its own.”

The Commentary on the Words of the Text elaborates the meaning of Kun's constancy: its substance is wondrous in nonaction, and its operation becomes manifest in action. For the nonaction of its substance is compliance; the action of its operation is vigor. Compliant and also vigorous—is this not why, for Kun, the constancy of a mare is beneficial? The Commentary on the Words of the Text elucidates this meaning to the utmost! Formerly, when our Master composed his commentary on the hexagram judgments, he had already explained the meaning of Kun through the Way of Earth; in the Commentary on the Words of the Text he further elaborated…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
之謂夫坤以純陰而得名地以純陰而成體坤
之道即地之道也故以其質言之則極天下之
至柔墳壤不同而其質之柔則同原隰雖異而
其質之柔無異屈博厚於高明之下安然不抗
不違何柔如之柔則疑於不剛也坤柔矣而其
動未嘗不剛乾之所施盡發生而無遺悉持載
而不撓德合無疆華嶽峙焉河海振焉非剛而
能若是乎以至柔之體而有動剛之用坤果一
於順邪以其性言之則極天下之至靜崗阜雖
===
殊而其性之靜不殊陵谷不同而其性之靜則
同泯生意於大塊之中寂然無聲無臭何靜似
之靜則疑於不方也坤靜矣而其德未嘗不方
乾之所始作其成而有常代其終而不易曲成
萬物植者植焉動者動焉非方而能若此乎以
至靜之性而有德方之用坤果止於順邪吁文
言以至柔至靜言坤之體而以動剛德方著坤
之用則牝馬之貞之意不既昭然矣乎嗟夫坤
者乾之對也夫子於乾則曰剛曰動而不言柔
punctuated: 之，謂夫坤以純陰而得名，地以純陰而成體，坤之道即地之道也。故以其質言之，則極天下之至柔。墳壤不同，而其質之柔則同；原隰雖異，而其質之柔無異。屈博厚於高明之下，安然不抗不違，何柔如之？柔則疑於不剛也。坤柔矣，而其動未嘗不剛。乾之所施，盡發生而無遺，悉持載而不撓。德合無疆，華嶽峙焉，河海振焉，非剛而能若是乎？以至柔之體而有動剛之用，坤果一於順邪？以其性言之，則極天下之至靜。崗阜雖殊，而其性之靜不殊；陵谷不同，而其性之靜則同。泯生意於大塊之中，寂然無聲無臭，何靜似之？靜則疑於不方也。坤靜矣，而其德未嘗不方。乾之所始，作其成而有常，代其終而不易。曲成萬物，植者植焉，動者動焉，非方而能若此乎？以至靜之性而有德方之用，坤果止於順邪？吁！《文言》以至柔至靜言坤之體，而以動剛德方著坤之用，則牝馬之貞之意不既昭然矣乎？嗟夫！坤者，乾之對也。夫子於乾則曰剛曰動，而不言柔
translation_en:
…this further, saying that Kun takes its name from pure yin, while earth takes its substantial form from pure yin: the way of Kun is precisely the way of earth. Thus, considered in terms of its substance, it reaches the utmost softness in the world. Though mounds and soils differ, their substance is alike in softness; though uplands and lowlands differ, the softness of their substance does not differ. It subordinates its breadth and depth to heaven’s height and brilliance, resting content without resistance or opposition. What softness could equal this? Yet softness might seem to imply a lack of firmness. Kun is soft, but in its movement it is invariably firm. Whatever Qian bestows, it brings forth and nurtures without omission, supporting and bearing everything without yielding. Its potency accords with the boundless: Mount Hua and the great peaks stand erect upon it, and rivers and seas surge upon it. Could it accomplish this without firmness? With an underlying constitution of utmost softness, it nevertheless functions with firmness in movement. Is Kun, then, exclusively compliant?

Considered in terms of its nature, it reaches the utmost stillness in the world. Though ridges and hills differ, the stillness of their nature does not differ; though heights and valleys are unlike, their nature is alike in stillness. It conceals the impulse of life within the great mass of earth, silent, without sound or scent. What stillness could compare with this? Yet stillness might seem to imply a lack of squareness. Kun is still, but its potency is invariably square—that is, regular and rightly ordered. Whatever Qian initiates, it brings to completion with constancy, carrying it through to its end on Qian’s behalf without deviation. It brings the myriad things to fulfillment according to their particular circumstances: rooted things take root, and moving things move. Could it accomplish this without squareness? With a nature of utmost stillness, it nevertheless functions with squareness in its potency. Does Kun, then, amount only to compliance?

Ah! The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) describes Kun’s underlying constitution in terms of utmost softness and stillness, while revealing its functioning through firmness in movement and squareness in potency. Is not the meaning of “the constancy of a mare” thereby made fully manifest? Alas! Kun is the counterpart of Qian. Of Qian, the Master speaks of firmness and movement, but does not speak of softness…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
與靜於坤既曰柔曰靜而又言剛與方何也蓋
陰陽本一氣乾得其全而坤得其半乾不必言
柔靜而柔靜在其中坤則嫌於偏也故又以其
發用者言之以見其爲乾之配耳聖人之言豈
偶然哉
易有聖人之道四焉者此之謂也
同考試官訓導王　批〔題意本多頭緒此篇鎔〕〔劇爲約非得於幾深之妙者不能言之吾爲子屬目矣〕
吏麟
===
同考試官教諭李　批〔此題通篇大旨歸宿處〕〔也是能約而言之無一贅語意其人必沉酣於是經者〕
〔或有得於蜀之隱君子者歟〕
考試官教諭丘　批〔會博於約傑作也〕
考試官教授陳　批〔文有源委〕
大傳結言易具聖道非一端即其所歷陳者是
已蓋辭占象變四者皆聖人之道也大傳歷陳
其義於前而復結言於此示人之旨何深切欵
□聖人之意盡於易聖人之道存乎書故以易
punctuated:
與靜；於坤既曰柔曰靜，而又言剛與方，何也？蓋陰陽本一氣，乾得其全，而坤得其半。乾不必言柔靜，而柔靜在其中；坤則嫌於偏也，故又以其發用者言之，以見其爲乾之配耳。聖人之言豈偶然哉！

易有聖人之道四焉者，此之謂也。

同考試官訓導王　批〔題意本多頭緒，此篇鎔〕〔劇爲約，非得於幾深之妙者不能言之。吾爲子屬目矣。〕

吏麟

同考試官教諭李　批〔此題通篇大旨歸宿處〕〔也，是能約而言之，無一贅語，意其人必沉酣於是經者。〕〔或有得於蜀之隱君子者歟？〕

考試官教諭丘　批〔會博於約，傑作也。〕

考試官教授陳　批〔文有源委。〕

大傳結言易具聖道非一端，即其所歷陳者是已。蓋辭、占、象、變四者，皆聖人之道也。大傳歷陳其義於前，而復結言於此，示人之旨何深切欵□！聖人之意盡於易，聖人之道存乎書，故以易
translation_en:
…and stillness; yet of Kun he has already spoken of yielding and stillness, and then speaks also of firmness and squareness. Why is this? Yin and yang are fundamentally one vital force. Qian obtains its entirety, whereas Kun obtains half. Of Qian there is no need to mention yielding and stillness, for yielding and stillness are already contained within it. Kun, however, might seem one-sided; thus he also speaks of its manifestation in operation, showing thereby that it is Qian’s counterpart. Could the sage’s words be merely incidental?

“This is what is meant by saying that the Changes contains four ways of the sages.”

Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The topic inherently has many threads. This essay condenses their complexity into brevity [?]. Only someone who has grasped the subtle wonders of incipience and profundity could express this. I shall keep my eye on you.”

Li Lin [?]

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “This topic is where the central purport of the entire text comes to rest. This writer expresses it concisely, without a single superfluous phrase. I imagine he must be deeply steeped in this classic. Perhaps he has learned something from a gentleman living in retirement in Shu?”

Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: “Bringing breadth together in brevity: a masterpiece.”

Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “The essay has a clear source and course of development.”

The Great Commentary concludes by saying that the Changes embodies the sages’ Way in more than one aspect: these are precisely the aspects it has enumerated. For statements, divination, images, and changes are all ways of the sages. The Great Commentary sets forth their meanings in succession above, then concludes with these words here. How profound, earnest, and sincere [?] is its intention in instructing people! The sages’ intentions are fully expressed in the Changes; the sages’ Way resides in the book. Thus, taking the Changes…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
書言之著卦設而後有象有變象變非伏羲之
道發於易者乎彖爻係而後有辭有占辭占非
文王周公之道發於易者乎是易成於三聖而
道發於四端故尚乎辭占而極天下之至精尚
乎象變而極天下之至變而其所以爲精爲變
者不有待於寂然不動感而遂通之神邪至精
極深而有以通天下之志至變研幾而有以成
天下之務而其所以通志成務者不有待於不
疾而速不行而至之神邪然則易有聖人之道
===
四焉者其此辭占之至精極深通志而皆本於
至神之謂也舍此奚有所謂聖人之道焉亦此
象變之至變研幾成務而皆本於至神之謂也
外此何有所謂聖人之道焉然則易道之大固
無不該而其用不外辭占象變四者而已君子
其亦當知所務歟抑大傳是章蓋承上章之意
而推言之也上章言天地大衍之數揲蓍求卦
之法辭占象變之所由本也此章言辭占象變
之用數法之所由行也然皆非人力之所能爲
punctuated: 書言之著，卦設而後有象有變，象變非伏羲之道發於易者乎？彖爻係而後有辭有占，辭占非文王周公之道發於易者乎？是易成於三聖，而道發於四端。故尚乎辭占而極天下之至精，尚乎象變而極天下之至變。而其所以爲精爲變者，不有待於寂然不動、感而遂通之神邪？至精極深而有以通天下之志，至變研幾而有以成天下之務。而其所以通志成務者，不有待於不疾而速、不行而至之神邪？然則易有聖人之道四焉者，其此辭占之至精、極深、通志，而皆本於至神之謂也。舍此奚有所謂聖人之道焉？亦此象變之至變、研幾、成務，而皆本於至神之謂也。外此何有所謂聖人之道焉？然則易道之大，固無不該，而其用不外辭占象變四者而已。君子其亦當知所務歟？抑大傳是章，蓋承上章之意而推言之也。上章言天地大衍之數、揲蓍求卦之法，辭占象變之所由本也。此章言辭占象變之用，數法之所由行也。然皆非人力之所能爲
translation_en:
…speaking of the Changes as a book, this is manifest [?]. Once the hexagrams were established, there were images and transformations. Are these images and transformations not the Way of Fuxi expressed in the Changes? Once the judgments on the hexagrams and lines were appended, there were statements and divinations. Are these statements and divinations not the Way of King Wen and the Duke of Zhou expressed in the Changes? Thus the Changes was completed by three sages, and their Way was expressed in four aspects. Accordingly, by esteeming its statements and divinations, one reaches the utmost subtlety under Heaven; by esteeming its images and transformations, one reaches the utmost transformation under Heaven. Yet does that which makes them subtle and transformative not depend upon the numinous power that remains still and unmoving but, when stimulated, penetrates all things? Through utmost subtlety, one plumbs the depths and can comprehend the intentions of all under Heaven; through utmost transformation, one investigates the incipient signs of change and can accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven. Yet does that which enables one to comprehend intentions and accomplish affairs not depend upon the numinous power that is swift without haste and arrives without traveling?

Thus, when it is said that the Changes contains four aspects of the sages’ Way, this means that its statements and divinations attain utmost subtlety, plumb the depths, and comprehend intentions, all rooted in the supremely numinous. Apart from this, where could one find what is called the sages’ Way? It also means that its images and transformations attain utmost transformation, investigate the incipient signs of change, and accomplish affairs, all rooted in the supremely numinous. Beyond this, where could one find what is called the sages’ Way? Thus the greatness of the Way of the Changes indeed embraces everything, yet its operation does not extend beyond these four: statements, divinations, images, and transformations. Should the gentleman not also understand where to direct his efforts?

Moreover, this chapter of the Great Commentary takes up and elaborates upon the meaning of the preceding chapter. The preceding chapter discusses the numbers of Heaven and Earth and of the Great Expansion, and the method of manipulating milfoil stalks to obtain hexagrams: these are the foundations of statements, divinations, images, and transformations. This chapter discusses the operation of statements, divinations, images, and transformations: through these, the numbers and methods are put into practice. Yet none of this can be accomplished by human effort alone…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
故上章則結之曰知變化之道者其知神之所
爲乎此章則歷推其義歸諸至神而復結言如
此則易之體用何莫而非神之所爲歟合二章
而觀之益可見矣
書

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “When a ruler emulates Heaven’s keenness of hearing and clarity of sight, proceeding entirely from impartiality, he accords with Heaven in virtue. This composition grasps that point.”
Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: “The passage on emulating Heaven is developed well.”
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “Concise and elegant.”

The Way of Heaven is wholly devoted to perfect impartiality, and the ruler takes its perfect impartiality as his model. For Heaven’s keenness of hearing and clarity of sight are nothing other than perfect impartiality. If the ruler models himself upon it and proceeds entirely from impartiality, how could he fail to accord with Heaven in virtue? title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
天下聽若與人邈乎不相接也然凡在覆幬者
皆其聰聞之所及天無目以下視若與人渺乎
不相通也然在化育者皆其明見之所逮善惡
之辨渾然靡隱之不爽雖有耳者不能及其聰
也福禍之降森然纖悉之無遺雖有目者不能
及其明也夫天之聰明如此無他公而已矣人
君位統萬方比之天道爲無異亦惟法天之聰
以聽乎天下凡其所聞不瑣瑣以爲智權馭八
表比之天體爲無殊亦惟法天之明以視乎天
===
下凡其所見不察察以爲哲好善惡惡之心以
公而不以私一天之於下民初不容心於其間
天之聰即吾之聰也賞善罰惡之典以理而不
以欲一天之於下人初不着意於其内天之明
即吾之明也天道至公而人君法之一無所私
則臣欽若而民從乂不期然而然矣大抵公者
服人之要道自家國以及天下未有舍是而可
以有爲者舍之則家庭之間道有不行而況於
遠乎傳說陳告高宗欲其至公以臨天下而且
punctuated: 天下聽，若與人邈乎不相接也；然凡在覆幬者，皆其聰聞之所及。天無目以下視，若與人渺乎不相通也；然在化育者，皆其明見之所逮。善惡之辨，渾然靡隱之不爽，雖有耳者不能及其聰也；福禍之降，森然纖悉之無遺，雖有目者不能及其明也。夫天之聰明如此，無他，公而已矣。人君位統萬方，比之天道爲無異，亦惟法天之聰以聽乎天下，凡其所聞，不瑣瑣以爲智；權馭八表，比之天體爲無殊，亦惟法天之明以視乎天下，凡其所見，不察察以爲哲。好善惡惡之心，以公而不以私，一天之於下民，初不容心於其間，天之聰即吾之聰也；賞善罰惡之典，以理而不以欲，一天之於下人，初不着意於其内，天之明即吾之明也。天道至公，而人君法之，一無所私，則臣欽若而民從乂，不期然而然矣。大抵公者，服人之要道，自家國以及天下，未有舍是而可以有爲者。舍之，則家庭之間道有不行，而況於遠乎？傳說陳告高宗，欲其至公以臨天下，而且
translation_en:
…to hear what is below [?], as though Heaven were so distant from human beings that it had no contact with them. Yet all who live beneath its canopy lie within the reach of its discerning hearing. Heaven has no eyes with which to look down, as though it were so remote from human beings that it had no communication with them. Yet all whom it transforms and nurtures lie within the reach of its clear sight. In distinguishing good from evil, its comprehensive discernment leaves nothing hidden and makes no error; even those who have ears cannot equal its hearing. In sending down blessings and calamities, its exact ordering overlooks not the slightest detail; even those who have eyes cannot equal its sight. Heaven’s hearing and sight are thus discerning for no other reason than its impartiality.

The ruler, whose position unites the myriad regions under his authority, is in this respect no different from the Way of Heaven. He need only emulate Heaven’s discerning hearing in listening to all beneath Heaven, without treating petty cleverness in what he hears as wisdom. His authority governs the eight outer reaches, in this respect no different from the encompassing body of Heaven. He need only emulate Heaven’s clear sight in observing all beneath Heaven, without treating minute scrutiny of what he sees as sagacity. His disposition to love good and hate evil must rest on impartiality, not private interest. Entirely like Heaven in its dealings with the people below, he must introduce no personal intent into the matter: then Heaven’s hearing becomes his own hearing. His established practices of rewarding good and punishing evil must rest on principle, not desire. Entirely like Heaven in its dealings with those below, he must introduce no willful intention into them: then Heaven’s sight becomes his own sight. The Way of Heaven is perfectly impartial. If the ruler emulates it without the slightest partiality, his ministers will respectfully comply and his people will submit to orderly government. These results will follow naturally, without being deliberately sought.

Generally speaking, impartiality is the essential means of winning people’s allegiance. From the family and the state to all beneath Heaven, no one has ever accomplished anything by abandoning it. If it is abandoned, the Way will fail to prevail even within the household—how much more so in distant places! Peng Rushi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “Although this topic consists of only three statements, writers find it difficult to formulate the transitions between questions and answers. Essays like this one are exceedingly rare.”

Yet they ultimately say nothing about ‘what is to be selected,’ ‘what is to be treated with reverence,’ and ‘what is to be weighed.’ This composition elucidates these points almost exhaustively. Moreover, it brings King Mu’s intention in issuing his instructions on punishments vividly before our eyes. For this reason it has been selected for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Qiu, Instructor: “Captures the intent of the instructions on punishments issued at that time.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: “Refined and precise.”

The worthy king posed questions and answers to elucidate three matters that bring peace to the people, wishing those who administered beneficent punishments to devote their whole minds to the task. When the feudal lords each devote their whole minds to these three matters, punishments thereby become beneficent.

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
有不擇則刑無所託要必擇慈祥溫良之士居
訊鞫聽斷之司然後刑可咸中民受其賜而國
享其福也爾所當擇者不在於人乎敬怠之際
治忽分焉固不容於不敬也然果安在哉蓋刑
有不敬則施或不當要必存寅畏恪慎之心於
輕重取舍之際然後刑可自慰民蒙其休而上
獲其慶也爾所當敬者不在於刑乎以至致詳
審之心於度量之間又果安在哉彼罪雖不出
於已身則已繫於獄所謂及也於此而不度之
===
則刑濫而民亦不安矣又必參其詞於兩造而
可刑則刑否則宥之有不計務使民心安而國
勢亦安酌其情於具備而可罰則罰否則赦之
有不嬿務使民命長而國祚亦長爾所當度者
又不在於獄之逮及者乎吁擇人也敬刑也度
及也皆安民之要諸侯能盡心於此民皆得其
安矣刑之爲祥也不亦宜乎抑考呂刑一書乃
穆王財匱民勞之日爲此以斂民財耳然其篇

punctuated:
有不擇，則刑無所託。要必擇慈祥溫良之士，居訊鞫聽斷之司，然後刑可咸中，民受其賜，而國享其福也。爾所當擇者，不在於人乎？敬怠之際，治忽分焉，固不容於不敬也。然果安在哉？蓋刑有不敬，則施或不當。要必存寅畏恪慎之心於輕重取舍之際，然後刑可自慰，民蒙其休，而上獲其慶也。爾所當敬者，不在於刑乎？以至致詳審之心於度量之間，又果安在哉？彼罪雖不出於已身，則已繫於獄，所謂及也。於此而不度之，則刑濫而民亦不安矣。又必參其詞於兩造，而可刑則刑，否則宥之，有不計，務使民心安而國勢亦安；酌其情於具備，而可罰則罰，否則赦之，有不嬿，務使民命長而國祚亦長。爾所當度者，又不在於獄之逮及者乎？吁！擇人也，敬刑也，度及也，皆安民之要。諸侯能盡心於此，民皆得其安矣。刑之爲祥也，不亦宜乎？

translation_en:
…if they are not selected, there will be no one to whom punishments can be entrusted. One must select men who are compassionate, kindly, gentle, and good to occupy offices responsible for interrogation, investigation, hearings, and adjudication. Only then can punishments all strike the proper balance, the people receive their benefits, and the state enjoy their blessings. Is it not people whom you ought to select? At the juncture between reverence and negligence, order and disorder diverge; one certainly cannot fail to be reverent. But where, precisely, should this reverence be directed? If punishments are not treated reverently, their application may be improper. One must maintain an attitude of awe and scrupulous care when weighing severity and leniency and deciding what to adopt or reject. Only then can punishments bring reassurance [?], the people enjoy their beneficence, and the ruler receive their blessings. Is it not punishment toward which you ought to show reverence?

As for bringing meticulous judgment to deliberation and assessment, where, precisely, should this be directed? Although the crime may not have originated with the person himself [?], he has already become entangled in a judicial case: this is what is meant by being ‘implicated.’ If one does not assess his circumstances at this point, punishments will be excessive, and the people will have no peace. One must compare the statements of the two parties: if punishment is warranted, punish; otherwise, pardon. ‘有不計’ [unclear: perhaps ‘without reckoning’]. Strive to bring peace to the people’s hearts and thereby stability to the state. Weigh the circumstances once all the particulars are available: if a penalty is warranted, impose it; otherwise, grant remission. ‘有不嬿’ [unclear]. Strive to prolong the people’s lives and thereby the duration of the ruling house. Are not those implicated in judicial cases the very people whose circumstances you ought to assess? Ah! Selecting people, treating punishments reverently, and assessing those implicated are all essential to bringing peace to the people. If the regional lords devote their whole hearts to these things, all the people will enjoy security. Is it not fitting, then, that punishments should be auspicious?

Yet, on examining the text of ‘The Punishments of Lü,’ one finds that King Mu produced it when his resources were exhausted and the people worn down, merely to extract wealth from them. Nevertheless, a spirit of compassion and solicitude [?] abundantly manifests itself in the chapter’s language; it speaks of employing people, of bringing peace to the people, …
