Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, School Instructor: When envoys receive their commands, they constantly fear falling short, lest they prove unable to fulfill their ruler’s intentions. The king describes this feeling as he sends them forth, and this composition succeeds in conveying it. For this reason it has been selected for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, School Instructor: This develops both the Zhou king’s intentions in sending forth his envoys and the envoys’ anxiety about neglecting their duties. If entrusted with a mission in the future, the author will surely be able to preserve this frame of mind and fulfill his duties. Accept it.

Comment by Examiner Qiu, Instructor: The writing is vigorous and forceful.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: It captures the meaning of sending forth envoys.

It is not just one man who diligently attends to his duties as an envoy; all share one mind in constantly fearing that they may neglect their duties. Such are the king’s words as he sends them forth. For an envoy’s duties are not easily fulfilled. As the king sends them forth, he praises their diligence and describes their concerns. How well he knows how to employ men! This ode about sending forth envoys says that, while the court’s solicitude is profound, its servants’ desire to render service is most earnest. These our…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
征夫有上介有衆介其行固非一人也莫不承
簡書之重而遂行於陛辭之餘有正使有副使
是行固非一職也莫不效協恭之誠而疾行於
祖餞之日釋殿庭之趨蹌勤道途之奔逐鑣相
聯而轡相竝也孰敢遲留也哉舍廟廊之逸豫
苒險阻之馳驅肩相摩而踵相接也誰敢濡滯
也哉然是征夫雖皆遴選之良也然志存乎立
功而欝抑于懷抱者常若有不能雖皆簡拔之
士也然事專於圖報而輾轉於思惟者恒若有
===
弗及上焉懷吾君一夫不得其所則德不下流
而朝廷委託之意無以副矣其心豈能釋然耶
下焉懷吾民一事不覈其實則情不上通而吾
儕瘝曠之責無所諉矣其懷豈能恝然耶恐恐
於君命之臨而憂其職之惟艱者衆介猶上介
也惴惴於從事之地而歎夫中之所有者明日
猶今日也吁惟其有靡及之懷此其所以無不
及之事也歟王者因以戒之如此辭不迫而意
已獨至矣大抵天下之事成於瞿而收於自滿
punctuated: 征夫有上介，有衆介，其行固非一人也。莫不承簡書之重，而遂行於陛辭之餘。有正使，有副使，是行固非一職也。莫不效協恭之誠，而疾行於祖餞之日。釋殿庭之趨蹌，勤道途之奔逐，鑣相聯而轡相竝也，孰敢遲留也哉？舍廟廊之逸豫，苒險阻之馳驅，肩相摩而踵相接也，誰敢濡滯也哉？然是征夫，雖皆遴選之良也，然志存乎立功，而欝抑于懷抱者，常若有不能；雖皆簡拔之士也，然事專於圖報，而輾轉於思惟者，恒若有弗及。上焉懷吾君，一夫不得其所，則德不下流，而朝廷委託之意無以副矣，其心豈能釋然耶？下焉懷吾民，一事不覈其實，則情不上通，而吾儕瘝曠之責無所諉矣，其懷豈能恝然耶？恐恐於君命之臨，而憂其職之惟艱者，衆介猶上介也；惴惴於從事之地，而歎夫中之所有者，明日猶今日也。吁！惟其有靡及之懷，此其所以無不及之事也歟？王者因以戒之如此，辭不迫而意已獨至矣。大抵天下之事，成於瞿而收於自滿。
translation_en:
…traveling envoys include a chief assistant and other assistants: certainly no one undertakes the journey alone. All bear the weighty charge of the written orders and set out after taking leave of the sovereign. There are principal and deputy envoys: certainly this mission involves more than one office. All demonstrate sincere cooperation and reverence, hastening on their way on the day of the farewell sacrifice and banquet. Leaving behind their measured steps through the palace courts, they diligently press onward along the roads, their bridles linked and reins side by side. Who would dare linger? Forsaking the ease of the court, they drive onward through perilous and difficult terrain [?], shoulders brushing and heels following close together. Who would dare delay?

Yet although these traveling envoys are all carefully selected men of worth, their determination to accomplish meritorious service leaves them burdened at heart, always feeling that something lies beyond their powers. Although all are men chosen for their abilities, their exclusive concern with repaying the sovereign’s favor keeps them turning matters over in their minds, always feeling that they may fall short. Above, they think of their ruler: if even one person fails to find his proper place, the ruler’s virtue will not flow down to the people, and they will have no means of fulfilling the court’s purpose in entrusting them with this charge. How could their minds be at ease? Below, they think of their people: if even one matter is not investigated to establish the facts, the true circumstances will not be communicated upward, and there will be no shirking their responsibility for neglect of duty. How could their hearts be indifferent?

When the sovereign’s command comes upon them, the other assistants are as apprehensive as the chief assistant, worrying about the difficulty of their duties. Wherever they carry out their work, they remain anxious and give voice to what fills their hearts, tomorrow just as today. Ah! Is it precisely because they fear falling short that nothing in their work goes unfulfilled? Such is the admonition the king gives them on this occasion: his words are not pressing, yet his meaning is already most profound. In general, the affairs of the world succeed through vigilance but come to an end through complacency [?]…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
則諫諫則有以備天下之闕是以自益天下之
事可幾而理也悲人臣奉君之命而致之必固
將聚百順以事之非細故也烏得不恐哉此周
王遣使臣必咨之以靡及之懷而繼之以咨諏
之務無是懷臣不能急是務急是務正所以濟
是懷也噫爲使臣者其必有所感而知所懼也
夫
君子之車既庶且多君子之馬既閑且馳
張選
同考試官學正鄭　批〔此篇車馬之盛誇於君前禮賢之意溢於言外宛如召公進諫之氣象也〕
同考試官學正魏　批〔意嚴而遂辭婉而難摸寫出老臣忠愛之悃取之〕
考試官教諭丘　批〔辭氣溫厚得告君之體〕
考試官教授陳　批〔文氣莊重〕
大臣極美王者來游之具其進諫之意微矣蓋
因事納忠臣子之職也召公從王游歌而極言
車馬之美如此欲王禮賢之意隱然於言外
punctuated:
則諫，諫則有以備天下之闕，是以自益，天下之事可幾而理也。悲人臣奉君之命而致之，必固將聚百順以事之，非細故也，烏得不恐哉？此周王遣使臣，必咨之以靡及之懷，而繼之以咨諏之務。無是懷，臣不能急是務；急是務，正所以濟是懷也。噫！爲使臣者，其必有所感而知所懼也夫！
君子之車，既庶且多；君子之馬，既閑且馳。
張選
同考試官學正鄭批〔此篇車馬之盛誇於君前，禮賢之意溢於言外，宛如召公進諫之氣象也。〕
同考試官學正魏批〔意嚴而遂，辭婉而難，摸寫出老臣忠愛之悃，取之。〕
考試官教諭丘批〔辭氣溫厚，得告君之體。〕
考試官教授陳批〔文氣莊重。〕
大臣極美王者來游之具，其進諫之意微矣。蓋因事納忠，臣子之職也。召公從王游歌，而極言車馬之美如此，欲王禮賢之意隱然於言外。
translation_en:
…then one remonstrates; through remonstrance one can remedy the deficiencies of the realm, thereby improving oneself, and the affairs of the realm may approach good order. Alas [?], when a minister receives his ruler’s command and carries it out, he must surely bring together every form of compliance in serving him. This is no minor matter: how could he fail to feel apprehension? Thus, when the king of Zhou dispatched envoys, he invariably exhorted them to maintain a sense of falling short, and followed this with the duty to consult and inquire. Without this concern, a minister cannot attend urgently to this duty; attending urgently to this duty is precisely how he addresses that concern. Ah! Those who serve as envoys must surely be moved by this and recognize what they should fear!
“The gentleman’s carriages are numerous and abundant; the gentleman’s horses are well trained and swift.”
Zhang Xuan
Associate Examiner Zheng, an Instructor, comments: 〔This essay extols the magnificence of the carriages and horses before the ruler, while the intention to have him honor worthy men overflows beyond the words. It has the very bearing of the Duke of Shao presenting a remonstrance.〕
Associate Examiner Wei, an Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning is stern and fully pursued; the language is tactful yet difficult [?]. It portrays the heartfelt loyalty and affection of an old minister. Accept it.〕
Examiner Qiu, an Instructor, comments: 〔The language and tone are gentle and generous, achieving the proper manner for addressing the ruler.〕
Examiner Chen, a Professor, comments: 〔The essay’s tone is dignified and weighty.〕
The great minister praises to the utmost the equipment for the king’s excursion; his intention to remonstrate is subtle indeed. For it is a minister’s duty to offer loyal counsel as occasions arise. The Duke of Shao accompanied the king on his excursion and in song, and spoke thus at length of the beauty of his carriages and horses. His wish that the king honor worthy men is implicit beyond the words.

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
召康公從成王游歌於卷阿之上因王之歌而
作此以爲戒上文以梧桐鳳凰起興至此若曰
君子當重熙累洽之日適民康〻〻之餘游歌
一舉何者而不備哉以其車言之左推右挽輻
輳於游歌之地者文采爲之交輝輕後軒前絡
繹於駐蹕之區者輪轅爲之相望九重之扈從
有以快群僚之偉觀嘽嘽嘽然數不可知而百兩
彭彭者難爲衆矣一代之制作有以萃百工之
所成焞焞然知不可詳而有車鄰鄰者実其多
===
矣是君子之車不假外求鸞輿之外尚餘也不
旣庶且多乎以其馬言之雲錦成群一皆調習
之素而鞭策之不勞驪黃奪目無非超逸之才
而控馭之不煩蕭蕭於轅軛之下者閑之維則
殆空冀北之群而跅弛之物無厠於其間焉伾
伾於驂服之内者範我馳驅誠爲神廐之良而
泛駕之馬無厰於其後焉是君子之馬無俟揀
閱龍馭之外皆馴也不旣閑且馳乎夫車多則
乘載有具馬盛則駕車有資車也馬也不知吾
punctuated: 召康公從成王游歌於卷阿之上，因王之歌而作此以爲戒。上文以梧桐鳳凰起興，至此若曰：「君子當重熙累洽之日，適民康〻〻之餘，游歌一舉，何者而不備哉？以其車言之，左推右挽，輻輳於游歌之地者，文采爲之交輝；輕後軒前，絡繹於駐蹕之區者，輪轅爲之相望。九重之扈從，有以快群僚之偉觀，嘽嘽嘽然，數不可知，而百兩彭彭者難爲衆矣。一代之制作，有以萃百工之所成，焞焞然，知不可詳，而有車鄰鄰者実其多矣。是君子之車，不假外求，鸞輿之外尚餘也，不旣庶且多乎？以其馬言之，雲錦成群，一皆調習之素，而鞭策之不勞；驪黃奪目，無非超逸之才，而控馭之不煩。蕭蕭於轅軛之下者，閑之維則，殆空冀北之群，而跅弛之物無厠於其間焉；伾伾於驂服之内者，範我馳驅，誠爲神廐之良，而泛駕之馬無厰於其後焉。是君子之馬，無俟揀閱，龍馭之外皆馴也，不旣閑且馳乎？夫車多則乘載有具，馬盛則駕車有資。車也，馬也，不知吾
translation_en:
Duke Kang of Shao accompanied King Cheng in roaming and singing upon the winding slopes of Juan’e. In response to the king’s song, he composed this poem as an admonition. The preceding passage introduces its theme through the images of the wutong tree and the phoenix. At this point, it is as though he says: “My lord, in these days of accumulated prosperity and enduring harmony, with leisure afforded by the people’s well-being [?], when you set out to roam and sing, what provision could possibly be lacking?

“Speaking of your carriages: pushed from the left and drawn from the right, they converge upon the place of your outing, their decorations gleaming against one another. Light behind and raised in front [?], they pass in unbroken succession through the place where your royal procession halts, their wheels and shafts stretching within sight of one another. The escorts of the innermost palace provide a magnificent spectacle to delight the assembled officials. So numerous, so numerous are they that they cannot be counted: beside them, even ‘a hundred carriages rumbling along’ would scarcely count as a multitude. The craftsmanship of this dynasty brings together the achievements of all the artisans. In their dazzling brilliance, they cannot be comprehensively known [?]; ‘carriages rumbling in throngs’ are indeed abundant here. Thus, my lord’s carriages need not be sought elsewhere: beyond the royal carriage, there are still others to spare. Are they not indeed plentiful and numerous?

“Speaking of your horses: they gather in herds like clouds of brocade, every one thoroughly trained, requiring no labor with whip or goad. Blacks and yellows dazzle the eyes, all possessed of exceptional ability, requiring no trouble to rein and guide. Those neighing beneath the shafts and yokes conform to the standards of training. They have all but emptied the herds of northern Ji, and no unruly creature is mingled among them. The powerful horses, both outside and between the shafts, ‘follow the rules in our galloping and driving.’ Truly they are the finest of the imperial stables, with no horse that breaks free of its harness following behind them [?]. Thus, my lord’s horses require no further selection or inspection: beyond those drawing the royal carriage, all are well trained. Are they not indeed disciplined and swift?

“Now, with many carriages, there are ample means of riding and carrying; with abundant horses, there are ample resources for drawing the carriages. As for these carriages and these horses, I wonder how our …

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
王將何以用之乎康公之意若謂是亦足以待
天下之賢者而不厭其多矣吁成王果能自悟
用是招來何憑翼孝德之不可得而壽考福祿
之不可致哉抑康公是言特因所見以爲戒耳
引而伸之位曰天位祿曰天祿民曰天民皆非
人君所得私也豈特車馬文具之末哉故載後
車者必寄以鷹揚之任錫乘馬者必委以屏翰
之拳此皆文實具備而爲王公尊賢者尚矣不
然安車蒲輪者竟何擀意於方行之一言耶此
又圖治者所當知也
===
春秋
蔡侯鄭伯會于鄧〔桓公二年〕
同考試官教諭白　批〔題本易見士子惟掇拾〕
〔事實襞積陳腐使聖筆爲中國懼弱示强之旨混聵不〕
〔明此作分剖詳盡鋪叙莊整殆謂以義理說春秋者可式〕
考試官教諭立　批〔說憂夏安夏最是〕
考試官教授陳　批〔辭義檃整錄之〕
李觀
punctuated:
王將何以用之乎？康公之意，若謂是亦足以待天下之賢者，而不厭其多矣。吁！成王果能自悟，用是招來，何憑翼孝德之不可得，而壽考福祿之不可致哉？抑康公是言，特因所見以爲戒耳。引而伸之，位曰天位，祿曰天祿，民曰天民，皆非人君所得私也，豈特車馬文具之末哉？故載後車者，必寄以鷹揚之任；錫乘馬者，必委以屏翰之拳。此皆文實具備，而爲王公尊賢者尚矣。不然，安車蒲輪者，竟何擀意於方行之一言耶？此又圖治者所當知也。

春秋
蔡侯、鄭伯會于鄧。〔桓公二年〕

同考試官教諭白批〔題本易見，士子惟掇拾〕〔事實，襞積陳腐，使聖筆爲中國懼弱示强之旨混聵不〕〔明。此作分剖詳盡，鋪叙莊整，殆謂以義理說春秋者，可式。〕
考試官教諭立批〔說憂夏、安夏最是。〕
考試官教授陳批〔辭義檃整，錄之。〕

李觀
translation_en:
…for what purpose will our king use them? Duke Kang’s meaning seems to be that these are sufficient to receive the worthy men of all under Heaven, without ever finding their numbers excessive. Ah! If King Cheng could truly come to this realization himself and use these things to attract them, how could he fail to obtain support for his filial virtue, or attain longevity, blessings, and emoluments? Yet Duke Kang’s words merely drew upon what he saw to offer an admonition. Extending their meaning, official positions are called Heaven’s positions, emoluments Heaven’s emoluments, and the people Heaven’s people. None may be treated as the ruler’s private possession. How could this apply only to such outward and secondary provisions as carriages and horses? Thus, one carried in an accompanying carriage must be entrusted with a charge requiring the prowess of a soaring hawk; one granted a team of horses must be assigned the responsibility [?] of serving as a protective bulwark. In these cases, outward form and substance are both fully present: this has long been esteemed as the way kings and dukes honor the worthy. Otherwise, how could the provision of comfortable carriages with rush-wrapped wheels ultimately convey [?] the meaning of the phrase “travel in every direction”? This, too, is something those who seek good government should understand.

Spring and Autumn Annals
“The Marquis of Cai and the Earl of Zheng met at Deng.” 〔Second year of Duke Huan.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Bai, Instructor: 〔The point of the topic is readily apparent. Candidates merely collect〕〔historical facts and pile up stale material, obscuring the intent of the Sage’s writing to express concern over the weakness of the Central States and show how they might become strong.〕〔This composition analyzes the matter thoroughly and presents it with dignity and order. It may indeed be called an explanation of the Spring and Autumn Annals through moral principle, and can serve as a model.〕
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔Its explanation of concern for the Chinese states and of securing their peace is especially apt.〕
Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: 〔The language and meaning are carefully ordered; include it in the record.〕

Li Guan

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
春秋於列國懼外也著夫自弱之由亦夫自強
之道觀書諸侯始合懼楚則夷夏盛衰之由安
夏待夷之道咸見矣世降春秋平王東轍令也
桓公初年蔡合鄭鄧始興講會之役共爲懼楚
之謀聖人因以協之著自弱而示自強者其意
云何以自弱之由言之楚地五千里帶甲數十
萬彼爲三國之見徒以萃聚壇坫而倉皇儀文
如彼何哉惟慮其小不可以敵大而泰山壓卵
之難支弱不可以敵強而羣羊搏虎之無計宣
===
王南征誰其續之尊號僭稱誰其革之江漢虐
焰將播煽於諸夏矣俱已見攝乎鄰壤而莫能
相尚卒之滅其國虜其君及終爲之服役信皆
有光於今日者然而中國所以衰夷狄所以盛
其由有如此寧不爲可戒邪以自強之道言之
天下莫大於理莫強於信義使爲三國之計畧
皆動循天理而惇尚信義夫何懼哉必期其小
可以大而興桑土未雨之思弱可以強而成虎
豹在山之勢南征之舉猶可復焉僭王之罪猶
punctuated:
春秋於列國懼外也，著夫自弱之由，亦夫自強之道。觀書諸侯始合懼楚，則夷夏盛衰之由、安夏待夷之道咸見矣。世降春秋，平王東轍令也。桓公初年，蔡合鄭鄧，始興講會之役，共爲懼楚之謀。聖人因以協之，著自弱而示自強者，其意云何？
以自弱之由言之，楚地五千里，帶甲數十萬。彼爲三國之見，徒以萃聚壇坫而倉皇儀文，如彼何哉？惟慮其小不可以敵大，而泰山壓卵之難支；弱不可以敵強，而羣羊搏虎之無計。宣王南征，誰其續之？尊號僭稱，誰其革之？江漢虐焰將播煽於諸夏矣。俱已見攝乎鄰壤，而莫能相尚。卒之滅其國，虜其君，及終爲之服役，信皆有光於今日者。然而中國所以衰、夷狄所以盛，其由有如此，寧不爲可戒邪？
以自強之道言之，天下莫大於理，莫強於信義。使爲三國之計畧，皆動循天理，而惇尚信義，夫何懼哉？必期其小可以大，而興桑土未雨之思；弱可以強，而成虎豹在山之勢。南征之舉猶可復焉，僭王之罪猶
translation_en:
When the Spring and Autumn Annals treats the states’ fear of external powers, it reveals how they weakened themselves and also the way to strengthen themselves [?]. In its record of the lords first joining together out of fear of Chu, we can see both the causes of the rise and decline of the non-Chinese peoples and the Xia states, and the way to secure the Xia states and deal with outsiders. As the age declined into the Spring and Autumn period, King Ping’s carriage tracks led eastward [?]. In the early years of Duke Huan, Cai joined with Zheng and Deng, initiating a diplomatic conference to devise a common response to their fear of Chu. The Sage accordingly brought them together [?]. What was his intention in exposing their self-imposed weakness and showing them how to strengthen themselves?
To speak first of how they weakened themselves: Chu possessed territory extending five thousand li and several hundred thousand armored soldiers. As the three states saw it [?], they could only gather at the meeting platform and fuss over ceremonial formalities. What could this accomplish against Chu? They worried only that the small could not withstand the large—as an egg could scarcely withstand Mount Tai pressing down upon it—and that the weak could not withstand the strong, with no more prospect of success than a flock of sheep fighting a tiger. Who would continue King Xuan’s southern campaign? Who would put an end to the usurpation of the exalted royal title? The flames of tyranny from the Jiang and Han rivers were about to spread through the Xia states. All were already cowed by their powerful neighbor, and none could rise above the others. Their states would ultimately be destroyed, their rulers taken captive, or they would end by serving Chu: surely all this was already foreshadowed at this moment [?]. Such were the causes of the decline of the central states and the ascendancy of the non-Chinese peoples. Could this fail to serve as a warning?
To speak of the way to strengthen themselves: nothing under Heaven is greater than principle, and nothing stronger than trustworthiness and righteousness. Had those devising the three states’ strategies ensured that every action followed Heaven’s principle and that trustworthiness and righteousness were earnestly upheld, what would there have been to fear? They should surely have resolved that the small could become great, taking thought to secure the nest with mulberry roots before the rain came; and that the weak could become strong, establishing a position like that of tigers and leopards dwelling in the mountains. The southern campaign could still have been renewed, and the crime of usurping the royal title could still …

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
可問焉江漢流毒亦斂跡於南荒矣自能保守
其國家而莫敢侮予要之國不至滅君不至虜
且不必爲之服役是皆可爲於當日者然則內
而安中國外而待四夷其道宜如此胡不知所
務邪吁不觀存會鄧之迹無以知聖人憂世之
心不觀抑會鄧之旨無以知聖人經世之畧然
而三國一會有關於天下之大故如此夫嗚呼
中國帝王所自立非夷狄所敢干也楚在商時
負險而叛已致中國之討矣至於我周而復封
===
之尋亦僭亂入春秋而萌蘖已成諸侯相攜而
懼之良可哀也已向非服之召陵挫之城濮則
將代宗周爲共主而爭長交見之事當不在襄
公末年矣故君子不得已而予桓文
楚公子嬰齊帥師伐鄭　晉欒書帥師救
鄭〔俱成公六年〕
周勉
同考試官𥘉諭白　批〔伐鄭救鄭一惡一善事理本自明白作者多惑於偏証互爲錯雜此篇講斷切〕
punctuated:
可問焉，江漢流毒亦斂跡於南荒矣。自能保守其國家，而莫敢侮予。要之，國不至滅，君不至虜，且不必爲之服役，是皆可爲於當日者。然則內而安中國，外而待四夷，其道宜如此，胡不知所務邪？吁！不觀存會鄧之迹，無以知聖人憂世之心；不觀抑會鄧之旨，無以知聖人經世之畧。然而三國一會，有關於天下之大故如此夫！嗚呼！中國，帝王所自立，非夷狄所敢干也。楚在商時，負險而叛，已致中國之討矣。至於我周而復封之，尋亦僭亂。入春秋而萌蘖已成，諸侯相攜而懼之，良可哀也已！向非服之召陵，挫之城濮，則將代宗周爲共主，而爭長交見之事，當不在襄公末年矣。故君子不得已而予桓、文。
楚公子嬰齊帥師伐鄭，晉欒書帥師救鄭。〔俱成公六年〕
周勉
同考試官𥘉諭白，批〔伐鄭救鄭，一惡一善，事理本自明白。作者多惑於偏証，互爲錯雜。此篇講斷切〕
translation_en:
…could likewise have been called to account, and the pernicious influence spreading through the Jiang and Han river regions would have withdrawn into the southern wilderness. They could themselves have preserved their states and ruling houses, with none daring to insult them. In short, their states need not have been destroyed, their rulers need not have been taken captive, and they need not even have been reduced to service. All this could have been accomplished at the time. Thus, to secure the Central States internally and deal with the barbarians of the four quarters externally, this was the proper course. Why did they not understand what they should strive for?

Ah! Without observing how the meeting at Deng was preserved in the record, one cannot understand the Sage’s concern for the world; without observing the intent behind his censure of the meeting at Deng, one cannot understand his strategy for ordering the world. A single meeting of three states thus bore upon affairs of great consequence for all under Heaven! Alas! The Central States were where emperors and kings established themselves; they were not for the barbarians to encroach upon. In Shang times, Chu relied on its defensible terrain to rebel and already brought punitive action upon itself from the Central States. Under our Zhou, it was once again granted a fief, but soon resumed its usurpations and disorder. By the Spring and Autumn period, these shoots had already grown strong, and the feudal lords joined together in fear of it. How lamentable! Had Chu not been brought to submission at Shaoling and checked at Chengpu, it would have replaced the ancestral Zhou as the common overlord, and its contest for precedence at mutual audiences [?] would not have waited until the closing years of Duke Xiang. Thus the gentleman had no choice but to accord approval to Dukes Huan and Wen.

“Prince Yingqi of Chu led an army to attack Zheng. Luan Shu of Jin led an army to rescue Zheng.” 〔Both entries are from the sixth year of Duke Cheng.〕

Zhou Mian

Comment by Associate Examiner Bai, whose school title is transcribed as 𥘉諭 [?]: 〔Attacking Zheng and rescuing Zheng: one was evil, the other good. The facts and principles are inherently clear. Writers are often misled by one-sided evidence and confuse the two. This essay’s exposition and judgments are incisive…〕

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
當且詞健氣昌卓有關鍵讀之自覺爽快
考試官教諭丘　批〔善發明傳意不𤰞爲事〕
實纏繞斯得謹嚴體矣
考試官教授陳　批〔責楚子晉體貼無遺〕
春秋於外夷虐貳而燕著其惡於伯國恤貳而
燕著其善此嬰齊爭鄭而伐喪欒書救鄭而還
師也比事以觀楚晉之一惡一善較然矣昔者
楚遣嬰齊以爲將適遇鄭喪而加兵自將以爲
有名矣經何以深惡之邪蓋荊楚僭王比諸夷
===
狄君臣大分之所繫也鄭能棄異即同是爲改
過而遷善矣楚果何義而敢來伐之邪不過問
埀棘之故泄蟲牢之憤以爲詞耳況悼公在殯
肉尚未寒桼何長驅而入利人之難以成其私
乘隙而來幸人之禍而逞其暴揆諸古之師不
伐喪者大相遠也是惡之中又有惡焉楚共君
臣燕有二惡如此容可逭其責乎故春秋直書
嬰齊帥師伐鄭若所謂不待貶絕而罪惡見不
貶絕以見罪惡是已於時晉命欒書以赴急及
punctuated:
當，且詞健氣昌，卓有關鍵，讀之自覺爽快。
考試官教諭丘，批〔善發明傳意，不𤰞爲事〕實纏繞，斯得謹嚴體矣。
考試官教授陳，批〔責楚子晉，體貼無遺〕
春秋於外夷虐貳而燕著其惡，於伯國恤貳而燕著其善，此嬰齊爭鄭而伐喪、欒書救鄭而還師也。比事以觀，楚晉之一惡一善較然矣。昔者楚遣嬰齊以爲將，適遇鄭喪而加兵，自將以爲有名矣。經何以深惡之邪？蓋荊楚僭王，比諸夷狄，君臣大分之所繫也。鄭能棄異即同，是爲改過而遷善矣。楚果何義而敢來伐之邪？不過問埀棘之故，泄蟲牢之憤，以爲詞耳。況悼公在殯，肉尚未寒，桼何長驅而入，利人之難以成其私，乘隙而來，幸人之禍而逞其暴？揆諸古之師不伐喪者，大相遠也。是惡之中又有惡焉。楚共君臣燕有二惡如此，容可逭其責乎？故春秋直書嬰齊帥師伐鄭，若所謂不待貶絕而罪惡見，不貶絕以見罪惡，是已。於時晉命欒書以赴急，及
translation_en:
…apt; moreover, its language is vigorous and its spirit abundant. It has a remarkably clear grasp of the crucial points, and reading it feels refreshing.
Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: 〔It ably elucidates the meaning of the Commentary, without descending into〕 entanglement in factual details. It thus achieves a careful and rigorous style.
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: 〔In censuring Chu and commending Jin [?], it fully captures the meaning, leaving nothing out.〕
The Spring and Autumn Annals makes manifest [?] the wickedness of foreign peoples who mistreat states that turn away from them, and makes manifest [?] the goodness of hegemonic states that show concern for states that turn away from them. Such were Yingqi’s attack on Zheng during its mourning, in his struggle to control it, and Luan Shu’s relief of Zheng and subsequent withdrawal. Comparing these events, the wickedness of Chu and the goodness of Jin become perfectly clear. Formerly, Chu dispatched Yingqi as commander. He happened to encounter Zheng in mourning and attacked it, himself presumably considering that he had a legitimate cause. Why does the Classic condemn him so severely? Because Jing-Chu usurped the title of king and ranked with the barbarians: at stake was the fundamental distinction between ruler and subject. Zheng’s ability to abandon the alien and join its own kind amounted to correcting its faults and turning toward goodness. What righteous grounds, then, could Chu possibly have had for daring to attack it? It merely used as pretexts calling Zheng to account over Chuiji and venting its anger over Chonglao. Moreover, Duke Dao’s body still lay awaiting burial, his flesh not yet cold. How could they [?] advance straight into the state, exploiting another’s distress to achieve their private ends, seizing an opening to invade, and taking advantage of another’s misfortune to indulge their violence? Measured against the ancient armies that did not attack a state in mourning, their conduct fell far short. This was wickedness compounded by further wickedness. With Lord Gong of Chu and his ministers guilty of these two evils [?], could they possibly escape blame? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals records directly: “Yingqi led an army to attack Zheng.” This is precisely what is meant by saying that guilt becomes apparent without awaiting explicit condemnation or repudiation, and that guilt is revealed without such condemnation or repudiation. At that time, Jin ordered Luan Shu to hasten to the rescue, and when…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
遇桑隧而遂還衆將以爲無功矣經何以深善
之邪蓋荊楚暴橫憑陵中國夷夏大防之所關
也鄭以即華見伐是因反正而受害矣晉方奮
義能無往救之邪正以撲江漢方張之焰分溱
洧倒懸之憂以爲名耳况繞角甫遇楚師已還
幸而謀定三卿而自以遷戮爲戒善惟從衆而
不以執俘爲功擬諸古之善陣不戰者亦庶幾
也是善之中又有善焉晉景君臣蕪有二善如
此寧可掩其美乎故春秋特書欒書帥師救鄭
===
者所謂凡書救者未有不善之也而伐者之罪
著是已吁鄭不當伐而晉國之師可舉鄭有可
救而楚人之罪益明春秋致謹於抑揚之間深
切著明矣雖然楚再伐鄭而勢益張晉再救鄭
而謀益協鄭能出幽遷喬善益著焉惜乎景公
信義一失而諸侯解體于蒲之盟不能尋馬陵
之約銅鞮之執無以挽重賂之成而鄭遂南向
不復貳矣噫此文襄之業尚當有賴於悼公也
䟦
punctuated:
遇桑隧而遂還，衆將以爲無功矣。經何以深善之邪？蓋荊楚暴橫，憑陵中國，夷夏大防之所關也。鄭以即華見伐，是因反正而受害矣。晉方奮義，能無往救之邪？正以撲江漢方張之焰，分溱洧倒懸之憂，以爲名耳。况繞角甫遇，楚師已還，幸而謀定三卿，而自以遷戮爲戒，善惟從衆，而不以執俘爲功，擬諸古之善陣不戰者，亦庶幾也。是善之中又有善焉。晉景君臣蕪有二善如此，寧可掩其美乎？故春秋特書欒書帥師救鄭者，所謂凡書救者，未有不善之也，而伐者之罪著，是已。吁！鄭不當伐，而晉國之師可舉；鄭有可救，而楚人之罪益明。春秋致謹於抑揚之間，深切著明矣。雖然，楚再伐鄭而勢益張，晉再救鄭而謀益協，鄭能出幽遷喬，善益著焉。惜乎景公信義一失，而諸侯解體，于蒲之盟不能尋馬陵之約，銅鞮之執無以挽重賂之成，而鄭遂南向，不復貳矣。噫！此文襄之業，尚當有賴於悼公也。

䟦
translation_en:
…having encountered the enemy at Sangsui, he then withdrew, and the commanders thought that nothing had been accomplished. Why, then, does the Classic so strongly approve of him? Jing-Chu was violent and overbearing, encroaching upon the central states: the great boundary separating the Yi peoples from the Xia was at stake. Zheng was attacked for drawing close to the Hua states; thus it suffered harm for returning to the proper allegiance. As Jin was now taking up the cause of righteousness, could it fail to go to Zheng’s rescue? Its declared purpose was precisely to quench the mounting flames of the Jiang and Han region and relieve the desperate distress of the Zhen and Wei region. Moreover, scarcely had the encounter at Raojiao occurred when the Chu army withdrew. Fortunately, a plan was settled through the counsel of three ministers. They took warning against transferring their slaughter to another target, followed the collective counsel toward the good, and did not regard taking captives as an achievement. Compared with the ancients who excelled at deploying armies without fighting, they came close indeed. Here was goodness within goodness. Duke Jing of Jin and his ministers possessed these two merits [?]; how could their excellence be concealed? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically records, “Luan Shu led an army to rescue Zheng.” This exemplifies the saying that whenever the Annals records a rescue, it invariably approves of it, while making manifest the guilt of the attacker.

Ah! Zheng ought not to have been attacked, and Jin’s army could rightly be mobilized. Zheng deserved rescue, and the guilt of Chu thereby became still clearer. The Spring and Autumn Annals exercises the utmost care in its censure and praise: its meaning is profound, incisive, and manifest. Nevertheless, Chu twice attacked Zheng, and its power grew still greater; Jin twice rescued Zheng, and its counsels became still more united. Zheng was able to leave the darkness and ascend to lofty trees, making its goodness increasingly apparent. Regrettably, once Duke Jing failed in trustworthiness and righteousness, the feudal lords fell away. The covenant at Pu could not renew the agreement at Maling; the detention at Tongdi could not reverse the settlement secured through lavish bribes. Zheng consequently turned southward in allegiance and no longer wavered. Alas! The enterprise of Dukes Wen and Xiang would still have to depend upon Duke Dao.

Postscript [?]

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
禮記
天尊地卑君臣定矣
顧㣧
考試官教諭丘　批〔說出聖人效法所本〕
考試官教授陳　批〔題本易見而難於作蕩〕
中士子每爲所窘理明詞順僅得此篇本房之冠無以
易子矣
兩儀異其勢禮制法其勢甚矣君臣猶天地也
聖人因其尊卑之勢而定爲君臣之禮何其效
法之善哉且夫治莫先於制禮禮莫大於君臣
===
聖人之制前禮也果何所法歟彼陽氣輕清者
爲天天位乎上其勢則尊陰氣重濁者爲地地
位乎下其勢則卑蓋天以乾健爲德日月麗之
而昭明星辰繫之而森列眾凡萬物莫不覆幬
於其下而其理則主於施而倡乎地天不亦尊
乎地以坤順爲德華嶽載之而不重河海振之
而不洩眾凡庶類罔不持載於其上而其理則
主於受而承乎天地不亦卑乎天尊地卑則截
punctuated:
禮記

天尊地卑，君臣定矣。

顧㣧

考試官教諭丘批〔說出聖人效法所本〕

考試官教授陳批〔題本易見而難於作蕩〕中士子每爲所窘，理明詞順，僅得此篇。本房之冠，無以易子矣。

兩儀異其勢，禮制法其勢。甚矣，君臣猶天地也！聖人因其尊卑之勢，而定爲君臣之禮，何其效法之善哉！且夫治莫先於制禮，禮莫大於君臣。聖人之制前禮也，果何所法歟？彼陽氣輕清者爲天，天位乎上，其勢則尊；陰氣重濁者爲地，地位乎下，其勢則卑。蓋天以乾健爲德，日月麗之而昭明，星辰繫之而森列，眾凡萬物莫不覆幬於其下，而其理則主於施而倡乎地，天不亦尊乎？地以坤順爲德，華嶽載之而不重，河海振之而不洩，眾凡庶類罔不持載於其上，而其理則主於受而承乎天，地不亦卑乎？天尊地卑，則截
translation_en:
Book of Rites

“Heaven is exalted and earth is lowly; the positions of ruler and minister are thereby established.”

Gu Yin 顧㣧

Comment by Examiner Qiu, Instructor: 〔Explains the basis of what the sage takes as his model.〕

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: 〔The topic is readily understood, but difficult to develop in writing [?].〕 Candidates are often stymied by it. Only this essay offers clear reasoning and fluent expression. As the finest essay in this examining room, yours cannot be surpassed.

The two primal powers differ in their positions, and ritual institutions take those positions as their model. How profoundly ruler and minister resemble heaven and earth! Following the exalted position of the one and the lowly position of the other, the sage establishes the rites governing ruler and minister. How admirably he follows his models! In governing, nothing takes precedence over instituting rites; among rites, none are more important than those governing ruler and minister. When the sage instituted the foregoing rites [?], what, indeed, did he take as his model?

The light and pure yang vital energy forms heaven. Heaven occupies the position above, and its position is therefore exalted. The heavy and turbid yin vital energy forms earth. Earth occupies the position below, and its position is therefore lowly. Heaven takes the vigor of Qian as its virtue. The sun and moon cling to it and shine brightly; the stars are attached to it in their multitudinous ranks. Of all the myriad things, none is without shelter beneath it. Its ordering principle centers on giving and taking the lead in relation to earth. Is heaven not exalted?

Earth takes the compliance of Kun as its virtue. It bears Mount Hua without finding it heavy; it contains the rivers and seas without letting them leak away. All the many kinds of beings are sustained and borne upon it. Its ordering principle centers on receiving and following heaven. Is earth not lowly? With heaven exalted and earth lowly, there is thus a sharp…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
然之勢不易而自然之禮以肇聖人者出仰觀
於天法其尊而制爲君之禮君則爲臣之元首
俯察於地效其卑而制爲臣之禮臣則爲君之
股肱吾知爲君者端冕凝旒居南面以臨乎臣
巍巍穆穆莫敢仰視而傍觀一乾健之運於上
也君之位不於此而定耶爲臣者執圭秉笏向
北闕以見乎君翼翼皇皇莫不俯伏以鞠躬一
坤順之行於下也臣之位不於斯而定耶吁兩
儀異勢而聖人法之以制禮如此君臣之分豈
===
非天地自然之別乎抑論之禮之爲禮所以辨
名分定民志綱維世道其所係亦大矣豈私意
臆度之可爲哉故貴賤之分法山澤之高卑小
大之事法陰陽之動靜類聚群分以性命不同
在天在地法形象之殊凡其見於制作之間者
一皆天地自然之序也然非聖人心識其妙亦
安能致是哉故曰明於天地然後能興禮樂也
故孝弟忠順之行立而后可以爲人可以
爲人而后可以治人也
punctuated:
然之勢不易，而自然之禮以肇。聖人者出，仰觀於天，法其尊而制爲君之禮，君則爲臣之元首；俯察於地，效其卑而制爲臣之禮，臣則爲君之股肱。吾知爲君者端冕凝旒，居南面以臨乎臣，巍巍穆穆，莫敢仰視而傍觀，一乾健之運於上也。君之位不於此而定耶？爲臣者執圭秉笏，向北闕以見乎君，翼翼皇皇，莫不俯伏以鞠躬，一坤順之行於下也。臣之位不於斯而定耶？吁！兩儀異勢，而聖人法之以制禮如此，君臣之分豈非天地自然之別乎？抑論之，禮之爲禮，所以辨名分、定民志、綱維世道，其所係亦大矣，豈私意臆度之可爲哉？故貴賤之分，法山澤之高卑；小大之事，法陰陽之動靜；類聚群分，以性命不同；在天在地，法形象之殊。凡其見於制作之間者，一皆天地自然之序也。然非聖人心識其妙，亦安能致是哉？故曰：「明於天地，然後能興禮樂也。」

故孝弟忠順之行立，而后可以爲人；可以爲人，而后可以治人也。
translation_en:
…their sharply differentiated positions remain unaltered, and the natural order of ritual thereby begins. When the sage arises, he looks upward to Heaven, takes its exalted position as his model, and establishes the rites for the ruler: the ruler is thus the head of his ministers. He looks downward to Earth, imitates its lowly position, and establishes the rites for ministers: ministers are thus the ruler’s limbs. I understand that the ruler, properly wearing his ceremonial cap with its pendants motionless, faces south to preside over his ministers. So lofty and solemn is he that none dares look up at him or glance sideways: this is wholly the vigorous activity of Qian, Heaven, operating above. Is not the ruler’s position thereby established? Ministers hold jade tablets and audience tablets and face the northern palace gates to appear before their ruler. Reverent and awed, they all bow low and bend their bodies: this is wholly the obedience of Kun, Earth, operating below. Is not the ministers’ position thereby established? Ah! Heaven and Earth occupy different positions, and the sage models his establishment of ritual on them in this way. Is not the distinction between ruler and minister the natural distinction between Heaven and Earth?

To consider this further, ritual serves as ritual by distinguishing names and stations, settling the people’s aspirations, and maintaining the order of the world. Its implications are indeed momentous. How could it be fashioned through private notions and conjecture? Thus, distinctions between noble and humble follow the heights and depths of mountains and marshes; affairs great and small follow the activity and stillness of yin and yang. Things gather by kind and divide into groups because their natures and allotted endowments differ; what pertains to Heaven and Earth follows the distinctions between images and forms. Everything manifested in the establishment of institutions follows, without exception, the natural order of Heaven and Earth. Yet unless the sage apprehended its subtleties in his heart, how could he achieve this? Hence it is said: “Only after understanding Heaven and Earth can one institute rites and music.”

Thus, only when conduct expressing filial devotion, respect for elder brothers, loyalty, and obedience is established can one fulfill one’s role as a person; only when one can fulfill one’s role as a person can one govern others.

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
余左之
考試官教諭丘　批〔冠義一題以責成爲主學者多失於泛此作得之故錄〕
考試官教授陳　批〔禮卷雖多言率膚淺殊不可人意晚得此作不惟見理精確而詞亦整飭可以爲文矣〕
善行備而斯可以成諸已已既成而斯可以責
諸人夫善行之備由於冠禮以責成之也然善
行備矣豈不可以成已而成人哉記冠義者推
===
先王重冠之故如此謂夫古人之冠也三加既
畢之後敬名易字之餘見於毋也兄也而責以
爲子爲弟之禮行見於君也鄉先生也而責以
爲臣爲少之禮行豈無自哉蓋以人能因冠以
明其禮因禮以脩其行處於內也篤天性之愛
敦天顯之倫以善事其父與兄爲則孝弟之行
自我而立矣處於外也效忠貞之節崇謙遜之
風以善事其君與長焉則忠順之行於我而脩
矣夫孝弟既立則親親之有倫而爲子爲弟之
punctuated:
余左之。

考試官教諭丘　批〔冠義一題，以責成爲主。學者多失於泛，此作得之，故錄。〕

考試官教授陳　批〔禮卷雖多，言率膚淺，殊不可人意。晚得此作，不惟見理精確，而詞亦整飭，可以爲文矣。〕

善行備，而斯可以成諸已；已既成，而斯可以責諸人。夫善行之備，由於冠禮以責成之也。然善行備矣，豈不可以成已而成人哉？記冠義者，推先王重冠之故如此。謂夫古人之冠也，三加既畢之後，敬名易字之餘，見於毋也、兄也，而責以爲子爲弟之禮行；見於君也、鄉先生也，而責以爲臣爲少之禮行，豈無自哉？蓋以人能因冠以明其禮，因禮以脩其行。處於內也，篤天性之愛，敦天顯之倫，以善事其父與兄爲則，孝弟之行自我而立矣；處於外也，效忠貞之節，崇謙遜之風，以善事其君與長焉，則忠順之行於我而脩矣。夫孝弟既立，則親親之有倫，而爲子爲弟之
translation_en:
Yu Zuozhi.

Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic from “The Meaning of the Capping Ceremony” centers on holding a person accountable as an adult. Candidates often err by treating it too generally. This essay grasps the point, and so it has been selected.〕

Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: 〔Although there were many papers on the Book of Rites, their arguments were mostly superficial and quite unsatisfactory. I came upon this essay late in the reading: its understanding of principle is precise, and its language is orderly and disciplined. This deserves to be called a well-crafted essay.〕

Only when good conduct is complete can one perfect oneself; only after perfecting oneself can one demand the same of others. The completeness of good conduct comes from the capping ceremony, which holds a person accountable as an adult. Once good conduct is complete, can one not perfect oneself and bring others to perfection? Such is the explanation given by the author of “The Meaning of the Capping Ceremony” for the former kings’ emphasis on capping. When the ancients underwent capping, after the three successive bestowals of the cap had been completed, and after their personal name had been accorded respect and replaced in use by a courtesy name, they presented themselves to their mother [?] and elder brothers and were charged with the ritual conduct proper to sons and younger brothers. They presented themselves to their ruler and the elders of their community and were charged with the ritual conduct proper to subjects and juniors. Surely this had its reasons.

Through capping, a person can understand the rites proper to him, and through those rites cultivate his conduct. Within the family, he deepens his natural affection and strengthens the bonds made manifest by Heaven, taking devoted service to his father and elder brothers as his rule [?]; thus filial and fraternal conduct becomes established in him. Outside the family, he demonstrates steadfast loyalty and esteems humility and deference, thereby serving his ruler and elders well; thus loyal and obedient conduct is cultivated in him. Once filial and fraternal conduct is established, affection for kin follows its proper relationships, and the duties of a son and younger brother …

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
職以盡忠所既備則貴貴長長之有序而爲下
爲少之職無虧善行立矣人道全矣仰焉無所
愧俯焉無所怍豈不可以爲人乎夫有諸己然
後可以責諸人由是舉孝弟之理而責夫爲子
爲弟者以亦能欲以啓其同然之天舉忠順之
道而治夫爲臣爲少者以未盡欲以觸其固有
之性以彼之善應吾之善導之而無不從率之
而無不化豈不可以治人乎是則禮行一備則
人已兼善冠禮所以責成人禮焉者豈徒爲哉
===
考之前章有曰禮義之始在於正君臣親父子
和長幼而責以三行者蓋責以成人之漸此責
以四行者責以成人之備是蓋冠者人道之始
嘉事之至重者也古人所以冠於阼階醮於客
位三加敬名之節筮日筮賓之事一皆行之於
廟無非愼重其事而責成之耳夫以人之待冠
者如此而人之當冠者宜何如亦曰體此而求
無負於加冠之意而後可
第貳場
punctuated:
職以盡。忠所既備，則貴貴長長之有序，而爲下爲少之職無虧。善行立矣，人道全矣，仰焉無所愧，俯焉無所怍，豈不可以爲人乎？夫有諸己，然後可以責諸人。由是舉孝弟之理，而責夫爲子爲弟者以亦能，欲以啓其同然之天；舉忠順之道，而治夫爲臣爲少者以未盡，欲以觸其固有之性。以彼之善應吾之善，導之而無不從，率之而無不化，豈不可以治人乎？是則禮行一備，則人已兼善。冠禮所以責成人禮焉者，豈徒爲哉？
考之前章，有曰：「禮義之始，在於正君臣，親父子，和長幼。」而責以三行者，蓋責以成人之漸；此責以四行者，責以成人之備。是蓋冠者，人道之始，嘉事之至重者也。古人所以冠於阼階，醮於客位，三加敬名之節，筮日筮賓之事，一皆行之於廟，無非愼重其事而責成之耳。夫以人之待冠者如此，而人之當冠者宜何如？亦曰體此而求無負於加冠之意，而後可。
第貳場
translation_en:
…the duties are thereby fulfilled. Once loyalty and obedience [?] are fully present, honoring the noble and respecting elders proceed in due order, and the duties of subordinates and juniors are fulfilled without deficiency. Good conduct is established, and the human Way is complete. Looking upward, one has nothing to be ashamed of; looking downward, one has nothing to blush for. Can one not then be a proper human being? Only after possessing these qualities oneself can one demand them of others. Thus one invokes the principles of filial piety and fraternal respect and requires sons and younger brothers likewise to be capable of them [?], seeking to awaken the Heaven-given disposition they share. One invokes the Way of loyalty and obedience and corrects subjects and juniors in what they have not fully accomplished, seeking to stir their inherent nature. Their goodness responds to one's own goodness: when guided, none fail to follow; when led, none fail to be transformed. Can one not then govern others? Thus, once ritual observance and conduct are complete, both others and oneself [?] become good. Surely the capping rite's requirement that one fulfill the rites of adulthood is not without purpose!
Examining the preceding chapter, we find it says: “The beginning of ritual and rightness lies in setting right the relationship between ruler and subject, fostering affection between father and son, and bringing harmony between elders and juniors.” Its requirement of three forms of conduct marks the gradual progress toward adulthood; the requirement here of four forms of conduct demands the full attainment of adulthood. Capping is indeed the beginning of the human Way and the weightiest of auspicious ceremonies. The ancients therefore performed the capping on the eastern steps and offered ceremonial wine in the guest's position. The observances of placing the cap three times and treating the personal name with reverence, and the procedures of divining the day and the guest officiant, were all carried out in the ancestral temple. All served to treat the occasion with care and gravity and to require the attainment of adulthood. If this was how others treated a person's capping, how ought the person being capped to act? Only by embodying this meaning and striving not to fall short of the intent of receiving the cap can one meet its demands.
Second Session

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
論
達則兼善天下
毛翥
同考試官學正鄭 批〔論塲博洽甚多但好異者語涉險怪其同者又不能陳言務去惟此作立意高古下筆清新胸中無限蘊蓄發明殆盡參之前後二塲〕
〔辭理俱優秋闈諸士當讓子出一頭地〕
同考試官學正魏 批〔題常則意新意常則語新古人作文之法也觀此論可以知其然矣青錢之選舍〕
===
〔子其誰〕
考試官教諭丘 批〔論題不隱而作近於釋者多矣是篇意古文奇讀之發人才思〕
考試官教授陳 批〔非茍作者尚允蹈之〕
時可以有爲也而能大有所爲斯古人所
以副天下之望矣夫能有所爲也而時不
可以有爲不得以有爲矣時可以有爲也
而不能有所爲不足以有爲矣可以有爲
得其時矣能有所爲得其人矣天下之人
punctuated:
論

達則兼善天下

毛翥

同考試官學正鄭批〔論塲博洽甚多，但好異者語涉險怪，其同者又不能陳言務去。惟此作立意高古，下筆清新，胸中無限蘊蓄，發明殆盡。參之前後二塲〕〔辭理俱優，秋闈諸士當讓子出一頭地。〕

同考試官學正魏批〔題常則意新，意常則語新，古人作文之法也。觀此論，可以知其然矣。青錢之選，舍〕〔子其誰？〕

考試官教諭丘批〔論題不隱，而作近於釋者多矣。是篇意古文奇，讀之發人才思。〕

考試官教授陳批〔非茍作者，尚允蹈之。〕

時可以有爲也，而能大有所爲，斯古人所以副天下之望矣。夫能有所爲也，而時不可以有爲，不得以有爲矣；時可以有爲也，而不能有所爲，不足以有爲矣。可以有爲，得其時矣；能有所爲，得其人矣。天下之人
translation_en:
Discourse

“When Successful, Bring Good to All under Heaven”

Mao Zhu

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, School Instructor: “Many discourses in this session display extensive learning. Yet those who seek novelty stray into precarious and bizarre language, while those who follow convention fail to make the necessary effort to eliminate stale expressions. This composition alone is lofty and antique in conception, fresh and lucid in expression. It brings out almost fully the boundless stores of learning within the writer’s breast. Considered alongside his work in the preceding and following sessions, both expression and reasoning are excellent. The other candidates in this autumn examination should concede that you stand a head above them.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, School Instructor: “When the topic is commonplace, make the conception fresh; when the conception is commonplace, make the language fresh. This was the ancients’ method of composition. Reading this discourse shows that it is indeed so. For the selection of a ‘bronze coin’—a candidate of unfailing worth—who could be chosen but you?”

Comment by Examiner Qiu, School Instructor: “The discourse topic is not obscure, yet many compositions come close to mere explication. This essay is antique in conception and remarkable in style; reading it awakens one’s literary powers.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: “This is no careless composition. May you truly put its principles into practice.”

When the times permit action, and one can accomplish great things, this is how the ancients fulfilled the hopes of all under Heaven. For if one has the ability to act but the times do not permit it, one cannot act. If the times permit action but one lacks the ability, one is inadequate to the task. When action is possible, the right time has been found; when someone has the ability to act, the right person has been found. The people of all under Heaven…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
固將傾心拭目以望其有所爲也古人於
此夫豈無所爲邪不獨善于一身必兼善
于天下而使天下之大天下之人之多皆
獲爲善人爲善俗則天下之望我者重且
大而我之所以副天下不亦重且大邪此
孟子達則兼善之言所以爲句踐告也非
爲句踐告也爲七國之諸侯告也爲天下
後世告也請畢其說大之生人厥賦惟均
人之有生所性皆善古之人知天之所以
===
與我者先天下而知也先天下而覺也而
天之望於我者覺天下之後知也覺天下
之後覺也由是憂勤惕厲恐不足以副天
之託而副天下之望也故君未我用也而
善以匡君之德義具矣國未我輔也而善
以輔國之德義具矣天下未我佐理也而
善以佐理天下之德義具矣君之知與不
知天下之知與不知固將囂囂也時或君
而知天下而知焉舉而在位焉陞而在
punctuated:
固將傾心拭目，以望其有所爲也。古人於此，夫豈無所爲邪？不獨善于一身，必兼善于天下，而使天下之大、天下之人之多，皆獲爲善人、爲善俗。則天下之望我者重且大，而我之所以副天下，不亦重且大邪？此孟子達則兼善之言所以爲句踐告也。非爲句踐告也，爲七國之諸侯告也，爲天下後世告也。

請畢其說。大之生人，厥賦惟均；人之有生，所性皆善。古之人知天之所以與我者，先天下而知也，先天下而覺也；而天之望於我者，覺天下之後知也，覺天下之後覺也。由是憂勤惕厲，恐不足以副天之託，而副天下之望也。故君未我用也，而善以匡君之德義具矣；國未我輔也，而善以輔國之德義具矣；天下未我佐理也，而善以佐理天下之德義具矣。君之知與不知，天下之知與不知，固將囂囂也。時或君而知，天下而知焉，舉而在位焉，陞而在
translation_en:
…would surely set their hearts upon him and watch expectantly, hoping that he would accomplish something. In such circumstances, how could the men of antiquity fail to act? They did not cultivate goodness in themselves alone, but necessarily extended goodness throughout the realm, so that, across its vast extent and among its multitudes, all might become good people and establish good customs. Thus the expectations the world places upon me are weighty and great; is not my responsibility to fulfill those expectations likewise weighty and great? This is why Mencius addressed to Goujian his statement that, when successful, one extends goodness to all. Yet he addressed it not merely to Goujian: he addressed it to the lords of the seven states, and to the whole world and later generations.

Allow me to complete this explanation. When Heaven [?; transcribed as 大] brings human beings into existence, their endowment is alike; all people are born with a nature that is good. The men of antiquity understood that what Heaven had bestowed upon them was the capacity to know before others in the world knew, and to awaken before others awakened. What Heaven expected of them was to awaken those who came to knowledge later, and to awaken those who came to understanding later. Accordingly, they labored anxiously and remained vigilant, fearing that they might prove unequal to Heaven’s charge and fail to fulfill the world’s expectations. Thus, even before their ruler employed them, they already possessed the virtue and righteousness needed to rectify his conduct through goodness; even before they assisted the state, they already possessed the virtue and righteousness needed to aid it through goodness; and even before they helped govern the realm, they already possessed the virtue and righteousness needed to assist in its governance through goodness. Whether their ruler recognized them or not, and whether the world recognized them or not, they would assuredly remain content and at ease. Should a time come when their ruler recognized them and the world recognized them, they would be recommended and placed in positions, promoted and placed in…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
職焉用而在君左右焉則陽德方亨而澤
加于民此其時矣誠思天下之大其人不
一也是故有淳者而不皆淳者而天下之
人之性不皆善也是故有厚者而不皆厚
者而天下之人之情不皆善也是故有得
所者而不皆得所者而天下之人之生養
不皆善也或可以爲善或不可與爲善而
其勢固不一也於此而欲其皆歸于善皆
入於善也豈易易識是必能全所得之善
===
而尊乎德焉安所守之正而樂乎義焉遵
是德德足以道天下矣遵是義義足以正
天下矣故幼而學者壯而行焉窮而學者
達而用焉以吾之所當養者君心也則必
養之以善焉君心者善之源也所當正者
朝廷也則必正之以善焉朝廷者善之本
也所當輔者國也則必輔之以善焉所當
佐理者天下也則必平定之以善而使天
下無不善焉國與天下皆善之推也君子
punctuated: 職焉，用而在君左右焉，則陽德方亨，而澤加于民，此其時矣。誠思天下之大，其人不一也。是故有淳者而不皆淳者，而天下之人之性不皆善也；是故有厚者而不皆厚者，而天下之人之情不皆善也；是故有得所者而不皆得所者，而天下之人之生養不皆善也。或可以爲善，或不可與爲善，而其勢固不一也。於此而欲其皆歸于善，皆入於善也，豈易易？識是必能全所得之善，而尊乎德焉，安所守之正，而樂乎義焉。遵是德，德足以道天下矣；遵是義，義足以正天下矣。故幼而學者，壯而行焉；窮而學者，達而用焉。以吾之所當養者，君心也，則必養之以善焉。君心者，善之源也。所當正者，朝廷也，則必正之以善焉。朝廷者，善之本也。所當輔者，國也，則必輔之以善焉。所當佐理者，天下也，則必平定之以善，而使天下無不善焉。國與天下，皆善之推也。君子
translation_en: …in office, and employed at the ruler’s side, then one’s yang virtue is flourishing: this is the time to extend its benefits to the people. Consider truly how vast the realm is and how diverse its people are. Thus, some are pure, but not all are pure, and the natures of the people throughout the realm are not all good; some are generous, but not all are generous, and the dispositions of the people throughout the realm are not all good; some have found their proper place, but not all have done so, and the conditions in which the people live and are nurtured are not all good. Some can practice goodness, while others cannot be joined in practicing goodness; their circumstances are certainly not uniform. In these conditions, how could it be easy to wish them all to return to goodness and enter into goodness? Recognizing this [?], one must fully preserve the goodness one has received and honor virtue, rest secure in the rectitude one maintains and delight in righteousness. Follow this virtue, and it will suffice to guide the realm; follow this righteousness, and it will suffice to rectify the realm. Thus, what one studies in youth one practices in maturity; what one studies in obscurity one puts to use upon attaining prominence. Since what I ought to nurture is the ruler’s heart, I must nurture it with goodness. The ruler’s heart is the wellspring of goodness. What I ought to rectify is the court, so I must rectify it with goodness. The court is the root of goodness. What I ought to assist is the state, so I must assist it with goodness. What I ought to help govern is the realm, so I must bring it peace and stability through goodness, ensuring that nothing in the realm is other than good. The state and the realm are both spheres into which goodness is extended. The gentleman…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
輔吾善也吾進之而君子不獨善其身焉
小人沮吾善也吾遠之而小人亦皆化於
善焉非仁不存所以養君心者善矣左右
皆善士所以正朝廷者善矣閭閻皆善俗
所以輔國者善矣人無不善而善與人同
所以平定天下者善矣蒔吾德焉而使天
下之大自朝廷而國而天下莫不遵吾德
焉遵夫德歸夫善矣廣吾義焉而使天下
之大自朝廷而國而天下莫不遵吾義焉
===
遵夫義入夫善矣性不皆淳者鑿之以善
而使性無不善焉情不皆厚者敦之以善
而使情無不善焉不皆得所者維持之以
善政而使之生養無不得所焉由是上而
吾君下而吾民堯舜其心而唐虞其風也
賡歌於上而擊壤於下也四方風動而萬
國咸寧也自東自西動無不準所準者此
善也自南自北思無不服而服者此善也
老者安之少者懷之自老及幼有以兼善
punctuated: 輔吾善也，吾進之，而君子不獨善其身焉。小人沮吾善也，吾遠之，而小人亦皆化於善焉。非仁不存，所以養君心者善矣；左右皆善士，所以正朝廷者善矣；閭閻皆善俗，所以輔國者善矣；人無不善，而善與人同，所以平定天下者善矣。蒔吾德焉，而使天下之大，自朝廷而國而天下，莫不遵吾德焉。遵夫德，歸夫善矣。廣吾義焉，而使天下之大，自朝廷而國而天下，莫不遵吾義焉。遵夫義，入夫善矣。性不皆淳者，鑿之以善，而使性無不善焉；情不皆厚者，敦之以善，而使情無不善焉；不皆得所者，維持之以善政，而使之生養無不得所焉。由是，上而吾君，下而吾民，堯舜其心，而唐虞其風也；賡歌於上，而擊壤於下也；四方風動，而萬國咸寧也。自東自西，動無不準，所準者此善也；自南自北，思無不服，而服者此善也。老者安之，少者懷之，自老及幼，有以兼善
translation_en:
…assist me in goodness: I advance them, so that gentlemen do not cultivate goodness in themselves alone. Petty men obstruct my goodness: I keep them at a distance, so that they too are all transformed toward goodness. I harbor nothing that is not benevolent: goodness is thus what nourishes the ruler’s heart. All those at his side are worthy men: goodness is thus what rectifies the court. Throughout the villages and neighborhoods, customs are good: goodness is thus what sustains the state. No person is without goodness, and goodness is shared with others: goodness is thus what brings peace and order to all under Heaven. I plant my virtue, so that throughout the vast realm, from the court to the state and to all under Heaven, none fail to follow my virtue. Following that virtue, they return to goodness. I extend my righteousness, so that throughout the vast realm, from the court to the state and to all under Heaven, none fail to follow my righteousness. Following that righteousness, they enter into goodness.

Where people’s natures are not wholly pure, I chisel them with goodness [?], so that no nature remains without goodness. Where their feelings are not wholly generous, I deepen them through goodness, so that no feelings remain without goodness. Those who have not found their proper place I sustain through good government, so that all find the conditions needed to live and thrive. Thus, from my ruler above to my people below, their hearts become like those of Yao and Shun, and their customs like those of Tang and Yu. Above, they exchange songs; below, they play at striking clods of earth. The four quarters are stirred as by the wind, and the myriad states all enjoy peace. From east and west, none fail to take this as the standard for their conduct: what they take as their standard is this goodness. From south and north, none fail to submit in their thoughts: what they submit to is this goodness. The aged are given peace, and the young are cherished; from the old to the young, there is a means to extend goodness to all…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
之也中國以安外夷以服自中及外有以
兼善之也而古人之道行矣天之所以生
者不負矣是豈假借於人而能若是哉幼
之所學者耳窮之所守者耳先知以覺後
知先覺以覺後覺者耳不但已之囂囂天
下之人傾心拭目以望於我大而重者今
果然矣則天下之人胡不鼓舞奔走以相
慰邪此非時可有爲而能大有所爲者邪
古之人有伊尹焉有傅說太公焉皆無意
===
於達也或感幣聘而禮之勤或因夢卜而
求之至起而用之於商周之世兆民允殖
惟民作乂四海永清皆其左右之力也兼
善天下惟斯人可以當之向使何人也而
可以語此然則孟子之言不爲天下後世
告邪抑遊說之徒古未之有也而戰國時
有之不徒有之也又從而相高之借使所
說者皆道德皆仁義遊說之可也今觀之
非功利則術數非戰勝則攻取而七國之
punctuated: 之也。中國以安，外夷以服，自中及外，有以兼善之也。而古人之道行矣，天之所以生者不負矣。是豈假借於人而能若是哉？幼之所學者耳，窮之所守者耳，先知以覺後知，先覺以覺後覺者耳。不但已之囂囂，天下之人傾心拭目以望於我，大而重者今果然矣，則天下之人胡不鼓舞奔走以相慰邪？此非時可有爲而能大有所爲者邪？古之人有伊尹焉，有傅說、太公焉，皆無意於達也。或感幣聘而禮之勤，或因夢卜而求之至，起而用之於商周之世，兆民允殖，惟民作乂，四海永清，皆其左右之力也。兼善天下，惟斯人可以當之，向使何人也而可以語此？然則孟子之言，不爲天下後世告邪？抑遊說之徒，古未之有也，而戰國時有之。不徒有之也，又從而相高之。借使所說者皆道德，皆仁義，遊說之可也。今觀之，非功利則術數，非戰勝則攻取，而七國之
translation_en:
…to bring goodness to them all. The central realm is thereby made secure, and the outer peoples submit; from within to without, all are brought to goodness. Thus the Way of the ancients prevails, and Heaven’s purpose in giving one life is not betrayed. Could one achieve this by borrowing from others? It is simply what one learned in youth, what one upheld in straitened circumstances: those who know first awakening those who know later, and those who awaken first awakening those who awaken later. It is not merely a matter of one’s own contentment. The people of the world turn their hearts toward me and wipe their eyes in eager expectation; the great and weighty responsibility has now indeed become a reality. Why, then, should the people of the world not rejoice and hasten to congratulate one another? Is this not to accomplish great things when the times permit action?
Among the ancients were Yi Yin, Fu Yue, and Taigong, all of whom had no intention of attaining high position. Some were moved by the gifts offered to recruit them and the earnest courtesy shown them; others were sought with utmost determination through dreams and divination. They arose and were employed in the ages of Shang and Zhou. That the myriad people truly flourished, that the people became well governed, and that all within the four seas enjoyed lasting peace—all this resulted from the assistance they gave their rulers. Only such men deserve to be called those who bring goodness to all under Heaven. Who else could have been spoken of in these terms? Were Mencius’s words, then, not an admonition to the world and to later generations?
Now, itinerant persuaders had not existed in antiquity, but they appeared in the Warring States period. Not only did they exist; they also competed to outdo one another. If what they advocated had all been the Way and virtue, benevolence and righteousness, itinerant persuasion would have been acceptable. Yet when we examine it now, their counsel concerned either achievement and profit or manipulative schemes, either victory in battle or conquest and seizure. And the seven states’…

title: 正德八年四川鄉試錄
text:
諸侯所繇道而喜聞者亦不過功利而□
矣術數而已矣戰勝攻取而已矣而吾道
德仁義之說以爲迂矣孰從而聽之宜乎
孟子以亞聖之才而負兼善天下之具而
不能一遇於諸侯也
表
擬宋趙汝愚進名臣奏議表〔淳熙十三年〕
楊愉
同考試官訓導王　批〔趙忠定公所編奏議在〕〔閫巳成至蜀上之可謂忠愛其君者矣此表能道此意〕
===
〔他日有言責必能言之士也〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔豐縟中寓典則意四六〕〔之善者也錄之〕
考試官教諭丘　批〔標著明白不冗不僻〕
考試官教授陳　批〔表語妥帖〕
淳熙十三年正月一日四川制置使兼知
成都軍府事臣趙汝愚誠惶誠恐稽首頓
首上言
punctuated:
諸侯所繇道而喜聞者，亦不過功利而□矣，術數而已矣，戰勝攻取而已矣。而吾道德仁義之說，以爲迂矣，孰從而聽之？宜乎孟子以亞聖之才，而負兼善天下之具，而不能一遇於諸侯也。

擬宋趙汝愚進名臣奏議表〔淳熙十三年〕
楊愉
同考試官訓導王批：〔趙忠定公所編奏議在〕〔閫巳成，至蜀上之，可謂忠愛其君者矣。此表能道此意，〕〔他日有言責，必能言之士也。〕
同考試官教諭李批：〔豐縟中寓典則意，四六〕〔之善者也，錄之。〕

淳熙十三年正月一日，四川制置使兼知成都軍府事臣趙汝愚，誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：
translation_en:
…what the feudal lords follow and delight in hearing amounts merely to achievement and profit [one character illegible], stratagems and calculations, victory in battle and conquest. Yet they consider our teachings of the Way, virtue, benevolence, and righteousness impractical. Who would heed and listen to them? It is no wonder that Mencius, despite his talents as the Second Sage and his capacity to bring benefit to all under Heaven, could not find even one receptive lord.

Memorial

This memorial conveys that intention.〕〔Should its author one day bear responsibility for speaking out, he will surely be a scholar capable of doing so.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔Within its rich ornamentation lies a sense of classical order: among compositions in four- and six-character parallel prose,〕〔this is an excellent one. Include it.〕
